There are many special stones, giving different amounts of points, adding lives, changing the size of the bat either to the good (bigger) or bad (smaller). The player have a certain amount of missiles, and some blocks can only be destroyed with missiles.

There are 32 levels to beat, with increasingly difficulty.

181570.overview:
Tarnak has finally been defeated and the curse of the demon has been lifted, saving the population of Kaldrion. Centuries have passed and the land of Kaldrion has become prosperous. But the ancient scrolls say that the evil one will rise again and the only way to stop him is to collect the twelve divine symbols that form Talmar's Wheel. This will ban Tarnak in his own world. It's now up to the player to go to the catacombs of the gods and find the symbols before Tarnak rises from his coffin.

Trapped is a first person role playing game similar to Ultima Underworld. There are four characters to choose from: Dwarf, Knight, Hunter and Fighter. Some characters are better with certain weapons than with others. Throughout the catacombs the player will pick up items that he comes across such as new weapons and potions that improves health, armour, strength and speed of movement. Spells can help the player along the way, for example a spell called Magic Map can be used to show where everything is. The mazes are complex and interconnected with stairs and teleports making each level massive in size and filled with all sorts of enemy.

181571.overview:
The sequel to Trapped is, like its predecessor, a 3D first-person action role-playing game in the vein of Ultima Underworld. The player character has a sword to attack the hordes of spiders, insects and wasps with, as well as fireballs which require mana. Plenty of other weapons are on offer throughout the lair the protagonist is initially trapped in.

There's a full magic system to get to grips with, and plenty of spells to collect, use and unravel. There are also puzzles that must be solved to advance. The game allows the player to save progress in one slot.

181572.overview:
Tricky Quiky Games: Die Suche nach den verschollenen Seiten is a promotional adventure action game by Nestlé, that was given free in Nesquik cereal packages.

The player must take control of Quicky the Nesquik bunny to recover pieces of the recipe to Nesquik cereal. The player must travel through a number of chocolate filled lands including forests, tropical jungles, underground, winterscapes, and the mountains. Armed with a small gun which shoots small red bullets, the player has a health bar represented by a bottle of chocolate milk, and takes damage when striking enemies.

181573.overview: Trivia Game Show is a Miscellaneous game, published by Impressions Games, which was released in Europe in 1991

181574.overview:
Triva Trove is a quiz game that consists of four parts that has to be completed in order. The first level is a variant of Tic-Tac-Toe played on a 3x3 board where each square contains a category. Upon choosing a category a four alternative question is given and if the player picks the right answer he gets a cross on the board and gets to choose the next category. If he answers wrong the computer will instead put a nought in the square. The game is timed and the first two levels have to be completed in twenty seconds.

In the second level the board is made up of eight circles with four subjects flashing on and off in sequence. The player has to stop the flashing when the chosen subject is black and then answer a question. Each of the four subjects have to be selected in turn which gets increasingly more difficult.

The third level is completely different. Here the player has to click on one of several squares that constantly change colour. The colours correspond to the ones used in a row of numbers at the bottom of the screen. The aim is to choose a square that represents a high number as possible.

The fourth level is played on a grid where some squares conceal jumbled up letters of a capital city. At the start the answers will flash and the player has to remember where they are. The player then has to answer questions to be able to uncover the squares and after each question the opportunity to guess the capital is given.

181575.overview: Trivial Pursuit: The Language Laboratory Edition is a Miscellaneous game, developed by Oxford Digital Enterprises and published by Domark, which was released in Europe in 1992

181576.overview:
In the second installment of the series you are entering the creation of Mr. Donald Trump - not only to play the casino games, but also to explore this "casino-resort by the bay". While playing one of the six games - Roulette, Blackjack, Baccarat, Slots, Poker, and Craps - you also may explore the Trump Castle's apartments, converse with its inhabitants, and even read the "Castle Courier" newspaper.

The game allows up to four players and may be saved in progress. The gameplay is directed on winning as much money as you can making the bets based on the combination of your luck and the theory of probability. You may be a millionaire.

181577.overview:
In this Mahjongg variant the player has to remove the tiles with the same marks from the board until all the board is completely empty. The elimination of tiles is allowed if these tiles are projected on the same line with no other tiles in their projection path. There are a certain number of same items on each level. The player can mark the tiles, or cancel the action to change the decision. The dead-ends exist if the strategy of tiles elimination was incorrect. Games are time-limited and a certain number of 'next move' suggestions are available during gameplay.

The game sports three difficulty levels as well as a 1 or 2-player mode. The best scores are saved in the high score table.

181578.overview: Turn It II is a sequel to Turn It. In this Shanghai variant the player has to remove the tiles with the same marks from the board until all the board is completely empty. The elimination of tiles is allowed if these tiles are projected on the same line with no other tiles in their projection path. There are a certain number of same items on each level. The player can mark the tiles, or cancel the action to change the decision. The dead-ends exist if the strategy of tiles elimination was incorrect. Games are time-limited and a certain number of 'next move' suggestions are available during gameplay.

181579.overview:
Tyran is an action adventure game. At the start the player may select one of three available characters (Mage, Warrior, Nobleman), all with different wealth, power, magic, range and possession status. Defeating Tyrant requires finding an hourglass, magic map, a book of birth and delivering them to the altar.

The tactical adventure part of the game features wandering through the land in order to visit different places (inn, mage tower, mage hut, altar, nursing home, old mine, castle, lake tower, forest tower) equipped with various goods and overcome the encountered enemies, guarding of useful items. Places marked with dots show the spots with enemies (red - three, orange - two, yellow - one). Entering such location moves the player to the duel action area. Both fighters are described by five factors: energy, stamina, strength, blow, resistance. The player may bring forth seven hits, use the block and escape the arena. Winning the fight is awarded with some useful items, loosing means a loss of gold. The travel may be shortened by the use of teleport holes. The character can be equipped with one of six types of swords and armors, ten types of spells, a few types of magical and medicinal items. A very important aspect of the game is a constant supply of food. Depletion of food automatically ends the quest.

184780.overview: This compilation contains Test Drive II and all released add-ons, which are the 2 car disks: Musclecars and The Supercars and the 2 scenery disks: California Challenge and European Challenge.

185129.overview: TaeKwonDo Master is a digitized fighting game. The game features three modes - single, duel (2 players) and tournament (3 to 6 players) and allows the player to choose one of six characters. Each character is described by height, weight and special blow and uses its own set of four unique moves. In contrast to the one year later released ECS side-scrolling version of the game, titled Super TaeKwonDo Master, TaeKwonDo Master uses enhanced AGA graphics and is played on a single screen board with 3rd-person perspective.

200913.overview:
Based on the ten pin bowling sub-game of the 1987 DesignStar/Mindscape C64/128 release of SPORTTIME SUPERSTAR INDOOR SPORTS (aka INDOOR SPORTS).
Ported from 1987 DesignStar/Mindscape Amiga release of the same game.

200915.overview: A remastered arcade quality port of Bubble Bobble by the Abyss and released as freeware in 2020. Like the original it is a platform game, with each level being a single screen. The enemies must be cleared from a level to go to the next one. With one player controlling Bub and the other controlling Bob, the player can jump and collect items for points (such as fruit). The real power Bub and Bob have however is the ability to blow bubbles. These bubbles can be as platforms to leap on, or to trap enemies. Enemies trapped in a bubble must be popped by jumping into them, wherein they'll turn to fruit. Additionally, power-ups sometimes float by in bubbles. They include lightning, which flies out horizontally at enemies, and water, which drags the player and enemies straight down flowing over platforms. Taking too long to complete any level will summon Baron Von Blubba, who will float around the screen trying to destroy the player.

201014.overview:
Following success with the mail-order Football Tactician series, Talking Birds entered the mainstream with this retitled version. It's a football management game, setting you in charge of one of the teams in the top 2 English divisions of the time and giving you control over transfers, tactics and training regimes as you aim to guide your team to success. Initially you can only manage the lower teams, but if you succeed over a few seasons you will become respected enough to have a chance to get the top roles.

The focus is on ultra-realism, which makes it very hard to quickly transform a club's fortunes, as there is a lack of money at many of the smaller teams and attracting players is harder than in the Premier Manager series and similar. Matches are viewed from top-down highlights, with 3 levels of detail (goals-only, highlights and kick-by-kick) offered.

201473.overview:
Turbo Sprint is based on the classic arcade game Super Sprint. The game features 8 tracks that range in difficulty; up to four players can control either a Blue, Red, Yellow, or Green car. Cars that players do not control are computer-controlled. When all 8 tracks have been completed, the game loops back to the first track, but the difficulty is increased. New players have the opportunity to join a race after each track has been completed.  

Turbo Sprint was created by the talented coder Graeme Cowie who brought us Rygar AGA and Bomb Jack Beer Edition. Looking to provide the best version possible of this great fun arcade on the Amiga, Turbo Sprint is designed to run on stock AGA Amiga including A1200, A4000, and the CD 32 peripherals disabled.

The original Super Sprint is one of those iconic arcade racing games from the 1980s that stood out because of its multi-player cabinet with steering wheels and featured well-balanced gameplay and striking graphics with miniature cars whizzing around twisty tracks. The game was originally ported across several home microcomputer systems, but an Amiga conversion was strangely absent.

201555.overview:
Tapper puts the player in the boots of a bartender who must serve eager, thirsty patrons (before their patience expires) while collecting empty mugs and tips! One game that many people remember so fondly that's all about serving patrons in a pub was that classic game 'Tapper.' A game by Marvin Glass and Associates released by Bally Midway, all those years ago in the Arcades in 1983. In fact, this game also appeared on the Atari 2600, Atari 8bit, Amstrad CPC, BBC MICRO, C64, MSX, and yes, even the ZX Spectrum. 
Old Bob has lovingly created a brand new version of "Tapper" for the Commodore Amiga,  requiring only an Amiga OCS with 1MB Chip Ram.

201572.overview:
Treble Champions is a football management game. The player can manage a squad, train players, and try to gain the way to the top of the leagues and cups. There are four divisions of 20 teams each and 1,500 (fictional) players with individual attributes are included in the game and purchasable for the manager. Beside the squad skills and injuries, the finances have to be managed for further progress in the game.

All menus and handling are presented in text based menus, mouse control is not supported. The matches are presented in text messages and an overview statistic about possession and shots. During the game, no interaction or intervention is possible. Loading and saving options are present. There are three difficulty levels and the player can chose in which league he wants to start (starting in the premier league is possible).

201573.overview: Treble Champions 2 is a managerial simulation in which the player takes over a team in the fifth UK division. The goal is to become successful in the Premier League in the long run. In comparison to the Treble Champions the options, previously restricted to training, lineup and transfer market, were expanded: now the player also may change the ticket prices, expand the stadium, borrow money from the bank and set up friendly matches before the season, Every athlete has a number of stats. There is no match presentation except a statistics field which gets updated over time.

201575.overview: Tracksuit Manager 2 was another game inspired by classic Championship Manager. It's the sequel to one of the finest football management games of all time.

205466.overview:
T.F.X. (Tactical Fighter eXperiment) is a flight simulation where the player can fly with F-117A, Eurofighter 2000 or F-22 Superstar in various scenarios as a UN fighter pilot. Before the player begins his/her duty, there is a need to complete 10 training missions. Only then will the rest of the possible game modes be available. The game also contains a mission editor where the player can create his/her own missions in any of the chosen scenarios.

The Amiga version was never officially released by Ocean. It was later included as a give-away game on a CU Amiga cover disk.

205599.overview: A tiny Space Invaders clone released to PD in 2020. Big fun in a tiny package.

205645.overview:
Trap Runner is a classic platform game with few twists. Mind traps, obstacles and monsters.

Beside the genre-typical jumping and running action you can cower yourself to avoid contact with low flying monsters. In later levels magic pills will help your task to save May. Collect potions to fill transparent ghost tiles with colour to make them solid. Other pills will change your own skin colour, allowing you to pass tiles with the exactly same colour.

Collect items to increase your score, gain extra lives or fulfil one of the special missions. Two of four levels a world have a mission to accomplish.

206819.overview: Tinyus is a faithful Amiga OCS port of the Arcade Gradius/Nemesis videogame It has been created by Fade1/aBYSs who is doing the graphics, Pink/ABYSs who is doing the music and code, Bartman/aBYSs who will be doing the reverse engineering, and all of this requiring an OCS with 512k Chip and 512k Slowmem or better! (Amiga 1200 (barebone) is recommended for fluid 50fps gameplay)

207228.overview:
Tex 07: El Morisco is an Action Adventure game, developed and published by Simulmondo, which was released in Europe in 1993. Tex Willer is the main fictional character of the Italian comics series Tex, It is among the most popular characters of Italian comics, with translations to numerous languages all around the world. ex is depicted as a tough guy with a strong personal sense of justice, who becomes a ranger (even if living in Arizona) and defends Native Americans and any other honest character from exaction and greed of bandits, unscrupulous merchants and corrupt politicians and tycoons.

Native Americans are portrayed in a complex way, emphasizing positive and negative aspects of their culture. The same can be said of the American authorities, like the U.S. Army, the politicians, the business-men, the sheriffs or the Bureau of Indian Affairs. 

In this episode, Tex 07: El Morisco, Tex is hired to arrest those guilty of a gun theft.

207229.overview:
Tex 8: Dramma Al Circo is an Action Adventure game, developed and published by Simulmondo, which was released in Europe in 1993.  Tex Willer is the main fictional character of the Italian comics series Tex, It is among the most popular characters of Italian comics, with translations to numerous languages all around the world. ex is depicted as a tough guy with a strong personal sense of justice, who becomes a ranger (even if living in Arizona) and defends Native Americans and any other honest character from exaction and greed of bandits, unscrupulous merchants and corrupt politicians and tycoons.

Native Americans are portrayed in a complex way, emphasizing positive and negative aspects of their culture. The same can be said of the American authorities, like the U.S. Army, the politicians, the business-men, the sheriffs or the Bureau of Indian Affairs. 

In episode Tex 08: Dramma Al Circo, Tex has to expose the perpetrators of some robberies.

207230.overview:
Tex 09: Il Fiore Della Morte is an Action Adventure game, developed and published by Simulmondo, which was released in Europe in 1993. Tex Willer is the main fictional character of the Italian comics series Tex, It is among the most popular characters of Italian comics, with translations to numerous languages all around the world. ex is depicted as a tough guy with a strong personal sense of justice, who becomes a ranger (even if living in Arizona) and defends Native Americans and any other honest character from exaction and greed of bandits, unscrupulous merchants and corrupt politicians and tycoons.

Native Americans are portrayed in a complex way, emphasizing positive and negative aspects of their culture. The same can be said of the American authorities, like the U.S. Army, the politicians, the business-men, the sheriffs or the Bureau of Indian Affairs. 

In Tex 09: Il Fiore Della Morte, Tex investigates some Indian deaths that seem to be related in some way to strange flowers.

210973.overview:
TURBO TOMATO is a high-explosive arena battle game full of frantic fruity fun for the Classic Amiga platform.

Fruit has never been so much fun!

THE GARDEN, a pastoral haven. The sun shines, the birds sing, the grass grows and the fruits, vegetables and other creatures live peaceful and happy lives. In this idyllic place live brother and sister Turbo and Nitra Tomato, enjoying the simple life with their friends.

But all is not as it seems...

Five a day? Come get some!

Take control of Turbo and Nitra Tomato in fast, one or two player co-op arcade action across four non-linear worlds. Use speed and sprouting explosive pods to do battle with increasingly dangerous mutant fruit and vegetable enemies - and other things. Gather power-ups and bonus items to increase your abilities and survive to continue the fight. Clear each level of mutants to progress and choose your route forward.

Can you uncover the terrible secret?

Can you save The Garden?
History

Brothers John and Adam Girvin first created the Turbo Tomato game in 1993, based on comic book characters Adam created while at school. It started as a homage to Psycho Pigs UXB (aka Butasan) but quickly grew in scope to the multi-world structure found today. Work continued until 1997, with a very rough and unfinished demo version being publicly released in December of that year.

Over the next 23 years, the idea of finishing a Turbo Tomato game never died and, though a few starts were made by both John and Adam, nothing was ever released.

In early 2020, John had just released Salitaire, a no-ads no-nonsense Solitaire game for modern desktop and mobile gamers, and was looking for his next project. Based on positive feedback received for the game at January 2020’s Amiga Ireland event in Athlone, Ireland, and on interest from publishers, John decided to resurrect Turbo Tomato one more time. And this time it would be different.

211188.overview:
One day a tiny leopard slug awoke from its slumber.

The grass was still moist from the morning dew, so it was a perfect opportunity too look around for food. Surrounded by this grassy area the slug was curious as to what it might find today for breakfast. It Passed by some dandelions, the slug was not interested. "Nah, not today" it thought, but a bright red fruit focused its gaze.

A strawberry, covered in small droplets of water. 'Woooah' thought the slug and headed towards it at a speed that only a stone might lose to.

The story for impatient players The slug is bored and is hungry for strawberries.
Go get that strawberry!

211216.overview:
A horizontally scrolling shoot 'em up created by Kevin Picone for Underware Design. Thesius XII is a challenging, high action, space fantasy shoot'em up. Thesius XII is similar in design to IREM's classic 'R-TYPE', although we consider it more a blend between that and my personal favourite, 'Silk Worm'

Thesius was re-released to feature three levels to battle through, each level is set within it's own unique scenario, containing various sound tracks and two major guardians per level. Throughout your battle, you'll encounter over 120 unique and highly aggressive alien objects, all of which, have one small idea on their very small minds, Destroy You.... (which is something they're very good at.. ;)

211269.overview:
Tales of Gorluth: The Tear Stone Saga is an action adventure in old-school retro style. The game sets you in the role of Karn, a young warrior who is on a quest in the land of Gorluth. In the introduction, we see Karn as a child in a classroom, being tought the history of an old war with the Elves. As the game proper starts out, Karn is now a grown-up warrior, returning to his home village after a long time of training in the capital Aasan, finding it in disarray after someone had stolen a valued statue of the village founder, and made off with it - to a nearby crypt. Now the villagers are unhappy and some have left the village to look for a better place to live, since who could stand having a villainous thief so close by?

So what is Karn to do now, with the thief long gone? Go search the crypt to find the statue, of course. While he tries, but fails to find the statue, someone in the village is kidnapped, and from there the adventure continues to save the villager, uncover the thieves hideout and explore the rest of the Gorluth world. The game is divided into three chapters: Turmoil in Middle Land, The Call of the Wild North, In the Lair of Evil. The story is told as text monologues by various side characters Karn meets, while the action is done by Karn on his own.

Karn is equipped with shield and sword, and the user interface shows his stats with a life bar and a shield bar, which can be replenished by finding power-up's and items on the ground or in chests. The action consists of walking around the underground or forest maps, using a single button to talk/open/examine/destroy/attack whatever is in front of Karn; it looks like Karn is throwing multiple copies of his sword toward the enemies, vertically, horizontally or diagonally. Some enemies only have close quarter attacks, while others can throw weapons across the screen just like Karn does. There are also quest items to pick up, that will carry the story further.

The game is a precursor to Tales Of Gorluth: Dungeon Of Reminiscence and to Tales Of Gorluth: The Legacy Of The Travelling Magician.

211380.overview: German language travel broker management game made by Jo Seitz of Sayonara and released in 1998.

211426.overview: You as a player, are a little fat ninja who needs to fight against old and creepy zombies and bats. A game created for the Capacitor Party 2019 and dedicated to the Amiga Community. A game by @edu_arana, with additional graphics by Andrea Zevallos and music and Fx by Carlos Gimeno.

211433.overview: ThunderDawn take the usual elements from RPG games and piles on the dark fantasy atmospherics. The result is a rather tasty full-screen experience. You are a brave hero-archer type who's been imprisoned in a sort of monster-infested maze by a rather unpleasant force. Your task is to escape by collecting a sufficient amount of Blood Crystals from the nests of a whole array of bone-rattling creatures.

211509.overview:
The honorable knight Mordred sets out to save his homeland from an impending invasion by the Occult Master, who rules over the neighboring lands of frost. Equipped with a sum of gold obtained from the sale of a magical artifact, Mordred must recruit fellow adventurers and complete the quests available in each city of the land.

Time Horn is a turn-based RPG with an overhead view. There is no character creation as Mordred starts with fixed attributes and so do any hired NPCs, though they all progress with experience. Trading, spells, melee and long-ranged combat are all on offer. The game keeps track of hunger and thirst for each character and it is crucial to their survival for all of them to keep a steady supply of food and beverages.

211515.overview:
A three person Tetris game. Amiga User International said it was the best game of its genre. Each player has a well in which to drop various shapes. The aim is to completely fill a horizontal row of blocks, which will then disappear, leaving space in the well. Completed rows effect other players, with single rows pushing others up, doubles producing green slimers, triples will releases assorted tricks and quads are especially nasty. 

Tritus was first released a few years ago as shareware.  Thank you to all who registered!  Now we've decided that you can have this full version for free.

Play competitively against computers or humans in this game with super smooth control and animation.  Your actions affect the other players.  Amiga User International said it was the best game of its genre.

211623.overview: Tetren is a public domain Tetris variant that can be played alone or with two people through split-screen. There is a password function, highscores and an option to toggle the music and effects.

211680.overview: Tajemnica Bursztynowej Komnaty or The secret of the Amber Room is an adventure game with graphics presented in the form of photographs. The action takes place in the surrounding countryside of the old palace. The main goal of the player is finding the famous Amber Chamber. The character may carry up to eighteen items that can be used and combined. The game screen is divided into inventory/action panel, commentary field and photograph showing the current location.

211707.overview:
TechnoVenture is a fun and innovative platformer with strong puzzle elements, similar to classic Apogee games of yore.  At first TechnoVenture might look like just another Sci-Fi themed platformer game, but closer inspection reveals it's actually much more.

The game begins with an advertisement for registration and the "Playfield" newsletter, which are quickly dismissed. You're not given any sort of introduction, but instead dumped right in the middle of the action. The "story", what little there is of it, tells you that you suddenly find yourself being a brand new XED-2000 robot, and your quest is to rid the land of the evil mutants. The story is told as you go along.

On the surface, TechnoVenture plays like a platform game. Your XED-2000 robot is subject to gravity, and can run on horizontal surfaces, or jump in the air. The physics model, while not entirely realistic, allows quite nice touches, such as being able to change your direction in mid-jump. While most of the action relies on well-aimed jumps, there are also items you can pick up and use, such as keys of three different colours, weapons, and shields. These come in handy when you're trying to kill the mutants or get past an obstacle. You can also collect money and purchase keys from the vending automats found in strategic places.

TechnoVenture isn't set on a series of levels or stages like conventional platform games, instead it has a big map made up of 100 fully interconnected "rooms", each taking up one screen. You can traverse these rooms in any way you please, providing the landscape lets you pass. There are also one-directional gateways and message boxes to help you on your way.  If all TechnoVenture had was one single map with one single quest, it would be quickly forgettable. Thankfully, this isn't the case. In TechnoVenture, the map is actually separate from the game engine, and other maps can be loaded from the disk, or even designed yourself.

211720.overview:
Terrahawks is an unofficial conversion of the Philips Videopac+ game of the same name (Called Attack of the Timelord on the Odyssey2 version). This was developed by Gary James and released into the public domain in 2017.

Game description:

The player has just attracted the attention of Spyrus the Deathless, the Timelord of Chaos, and his only defense is his Time Machine's laser cannon. The Timelord will now send his fleet of Time Ships to destroy the player.

In this space shooter the player controls the Time Machine horizontally with the directional stick and shoots its laser with the action button. The Timelord's Time Ships have four kinds of weapons to assault the player, and they will be introduced in the game's first four levels.

In the first level, the Time Ships will shoot missiles, which travel in straight lines toward the bottom of the screen. In the second level, the fleet will also use antimatter mines, which will follow the player's Time Machine movements. In the third level, the fleet will also use annihilators, weapons that will go straight to the bottom of the screen, and then try to hit the player from the sides. In the fourth level, the Timelord will also send Nucleonic Time killers, robot-piloted destroyers which can anticipate human actions.

The game has 256 stages of progressively increasing difficulty, with faster and better armed enemies. Each level is beaten after all Time Ships are destroyed.

The player scores 2 points for each missile destroyed, 4 points for each antimatter mine, 5 points for each Time Ship, 8 points for each annihilator and 16 points for each Time killer destroyed.

The Timelord appears at the start of each level, but his transmission can be jammed by starting the game pressing 0 (zero). This way he'll not reappear each time the player destroys a fleet of his Time Ships.

211753.overview:
This game is the sequel to Emotional Conflict. In that game you tried to hunt down Mutant Mickey, a head-case, but upon finding him, you let him slip through your slimy, greasy, oily fingers. Though you did manage to recover the rare, lost coin. And now we're back, back FOR REVENGE, I tell you. This time, MM has kidnapped your Mother and is holding her hostage in this maximum security hotel, where rich celebrities like Mikey stay. You begin in the lobby and begin your revenge from there! 
 
Game came packed with a sub game called Wormzies. Asa Margetts was the creator and developer of this overhead, point and click PD game.

211757.overview: A 2D, 3rd person graphic adventure game created by Andreas Falkenhahn in 1998.

211792.overview: Cannon Fodder clone with great support and an integrated level editor. A strategy shooter. You can shoot and throw grenades, and even fly around in helicopters and other things much later on. Make sure to get the latest version, earlier ones have a bug at level 3 that stops progression. I loved this, despite not being able to finish a specific level in which I was totally stumped on how to progress. The Turtleminator plays similar to Cannon Fodder, except you're limited to one player character. You and your enemies move faster. I think with a little more work on the graphics and with more levels, this could have easily been a commercial release. (note, the 1999 bug-fix edition had additional levels.)

211819.overview: Turbo Jam is a racing game where the player drives a car through a maze viewed from a top down perspective. The car is constantly moving forward and most of the player's control involve steering it left and right at intersections. It is however also possible to speed up and to reverse slowly. In each level of the game the objective is to collect all the flags which appear on the screen one at a time. Similar to Head-On there are chaser cars that are out after the player and it' necessary to avoid crashing into these. If that happens a life will be lost. To help the player it's possible to pick up fireballs that then can be launched and used to destroy the chasing cars.

211833.overview: Sequel to Testament, a horror-themed first person shooter with engine similar to Wolfenstein 3D. Game is basically the same as it's predecessor, but with new enemies, levels and few new textures.

211835.overview: The last in the Train Driver series, this one features dozens of routes across England and Scotland, with authentic sounding diesel and electric trains. Its tricky to start rolling, and difficult to know when to brake for stations, but it does give a warning if you missed one.

211838.overview: Originally released as a shareware game on Aminet in 1997, this game was slightly reworked and repackaged by well known nefarious ne'er do wells, Mediasoft and released commercially in 1999. Shipped in a standard CD-R jewel box with inlay created with a laser printer. This is a single player driving game where you avoid obstacles and keep your computer opponent (the blue cars) in your rear-view.

211872.overview:
WILIGHT KNIGHTS, the English version of RYCERZE MROKU, was scheduled for shareware release in 1997 outside of Poland, but never materialised. In 2006, however, the developers granted permission for the game to be made available for download.

Coding by Mariusz "MDW" Wlodarczyk. Graphics by Karol "Caro" Wlodarczyk and ASL; digitising by Tomasz Rogala. Music by Artur "Mobby" Pietrzak. 

Rycerze Mroku is a first person perspective fantasy martial art game. The goal of the game is to defeat the evil minions and save the world. Each duel is preceded by a text introduction and animation of opponent's skills. The fight itself takes place in a FPP one screen view. The player may release a few types of attacks and defensive moves. The characters are described by two indicators - energy level (falls after each hit) and the level of reflexes (falls during the attack).

211894.overview: So simple but fantastic fun. A shareware, 2-player split screen first-person shooter duel. You get some powerups like teleporters, invisibility, or fireballs by entering into the various doors in the arena. Hilarious death scene. Trick or Treat values gameplay over an advanced engine and is a fun texture mapped arena shooter for two players. Each player is allocated their own mini-view of the maze which allows simultaneous play.

211904.overview: A DynaBlaster/Bomberman clone without sound effects.  In Teddy, you and all baddies can walk through bombs. This makes the game more difficult. On the other hand, since every level fits on a single screen, planning ahead is little easier.

211922.overview: Spoof game based on the popular Teletubbies BBC TV programme. In this cross-hairs shooter you can get out your built-up Teletubby aggression. Time for Tubby Bye-Bye!!

211971.overview: A Space-Taxi style, 2D Reaction & Navigation game by Harald Müller (Mueller), published in 1995.

211972.overview: Released in 1993 as a PD demo where you could send in for the full game. It is a Frogger clonefor one player with a time limit per level to make things more interesting. Toado is a variant of Konami's classic arcade game Frogger. Although there is a few differences, Toado plays mostly the same as the original. The objective is simple: guide your frogs from the bottom of the screen to their home at the top. To do so you must pass in order, a road, a railway track, a lawn and a river full of floating logs. You have five frogs, and when all of them has reached safety, you will advance to the next level. In later levels the game will become tougher and not just because of the increased speed. You will come across new dangers to watch out for, such as a locomotive, a lawn mover and a tractor. A difference from the original Frogger is that there is a barrier in the middle of the road, making it a bit harder.

211973.overview: A clone of Locomotion coded by Barry "Dingo" Driver in Blitz Basic 2. Transport the passengers to their required destinations within the time limit using the Little trains.

212038.overview: This cool little 2D platform game is created with a game creator tool called Overbird. Which can be found on Aminet. The game is a pastiche of Tomb Raider, or at least presents itself as one. It features the busty heroine, Rhonda the Redhead as she progresses through levels beating up the aggressive men and other monsters she finds and kicking rocks out of her way, while squat thrusting to pick up treasures. The game has some simple puzzle and fighting elements.

212039.overview: Targis is an platform game with a look and feel reminiscent of Lode Runner, developed and published by Incognito, which was released in 1988. Brave the Proter's lair and retrieve all of the stolen rocket parts or have the terror of the Proters haunt the rest of the galaxy forever! 200 different levels of lair, full level editor create infinitely many levels. Player can modify all graphics, sound and animations to make Targis a totally difficult game every time. Incredibly addictive and endless hours of family enjoyment.

212040.overview: A top down turn based Laser Squad style wargame created by Mark Sheeky of Scorpius and released in 1993.  You have to control your team, equip them with various weapons, etc. Allied agents descend into enemy territory, ready for action. Agent ADAMS scans the area ahead with his cyborg eye. An armed figure is located by the entrance to the enemy complex, take him out before he has a chance to react. Your squad steps over the dead guard  and the task force enters the enemy complex anticipating strong resistance to follow...

212041.overview: You play as the iconic Leatherface from the Texas Chainsaw Massacre movie. Your objective is to kill as many hapless victims as you can before you run out of petrol for your chainsaw. There are petrol canisters that extend playtime in a single round. When you run out of petrol, it is game over and you cycle back to the title screen.

212042.overview: Tomten are Swedish gnomes or elves and Tomtespelet translates as The Santa Game. It is a 2 player only, split-screen, game with similarities to Air/Table top hockey games. The upper gnome has a white ball and the lower one has a red ball and each try to score simultaneously.

212043.overview:
Touch all colored tiles and go to exit. Fun little PD game. There's a witty double meaning in this title. You must guide a character from the start of a maze through to the end. The difficulty is that each square disappears after you step on it, meaning that you have to touch the square and go, without being able to return.

You're also up against a strict time limit, so it's all too easy to make a crucial mistake and be forced to step into oblivion. It's therefore definitely touch and go as to whether you can get through it.

212044.overview:
A RedPill based game which is for all Amigas with at least 2MB memory as a minimum. As noted by the developer this game was through the culmination of 8 months of intense work and is inspired by the classic game of Booby Kids which appeared on the Acades and the NES. 
In this game you must traverse each of the many screens to collect all the treasures which are scattered about the level to open up the doors to allow you to progress. Once that is done you can progress onto the next level and experience all 6 levels in the game to complete the game for good. Just be aware there are enemies about, that although can be avoided, you can also dig holes for them to fall in and be hopeful they disappear for good.

212045.overview: Tumbler Street is a miscellaneous gambling game, developed and published by Vidball, which was released in Europe in 1989. In it, the hoodlum hides the red ball under one of the 3 tumblers, and you have to guess where it is. If you guess correctly, you get some cash, incorrectly you lose. Randomly, the police will show up, and he will take off running...with your cash. The fact that this was sold commercially is a bit too on the nose.

212046.overview: An avoid-it style, racing action and navigation game created by Scorpius and released in 1992. Later deemed freeware by author, Mark Sheeky, on his old website and published through itch.io. Turbo Thrust had various roots of inspiration. Years earlier, I wrote a simple vertical scrolling game on Dragon 32, where a 'Y' flew down a tunnel, and this was a surprisingly addictive hit. Years later, Salamander on the Commodore 64 had a bonus level which involved flying along a tunnel at speed. I wanted to create a race game based on these principles. Early versions of the Turbo Thrust destroyed players when they hit the wall, but this made the game impossibly hard. The game is two player only, and each player uses a joystick. The fire button accelerates. There are no penalties for crashing except losing time.

212106.overview: An oddly addicting puzzle game developed and published by Logistic Dreams and features single and head to head, split-screen play, which was released in Europe in 1998. It is a precursor to Talmino 2.

212107.overview: . You move from left to right, collect diamonds, hop on enemies, and avoid spike or fireball traps. One difference to other platformers is that the player character can only jump, not walk.

212108.overview:
Top Tiler is an puzzle-arcade game with an idea in mind: to recreate the atmosphere of Japanese arcades we were used to see in the late '80s. The gameplay is very simple. To win, you have to move your character over the tiles in the background in order to reveal the image hidden behind them.
You have to avoid the roaming enemies too or you'll lose a precious life. Some tiles have special properties. The effect these tiles produce are described at the beginning of the game. The game has 6 levels, which are divided into 4 sublevels. It has a nice ending sequence with credits too.

212109.overview:
Total Pattern is a new game by Digital Team with 20 puzzle levels. The game’s preview had it’s debut at Retrokomp/Loaderror 2015 party. After that djpiotrs was joined by Selur, who created new graphics and Andrzej Drozd, responsible for the soundtrack. 
The game is based on Sokoban, but with some tweaks and changes.

212110.overview: A Czech game with many parts translated into English, this is a Tetris game with some bonuses and power ups. The game has 4 "game worlds" which correspond to 4 variants of tetris. Please note the menu has 20, but are not available in the basic version. There is no 2 player mode. A Czech editor is available by booting from floppy disk 4 to increase the number of worlds. Hard disk use is strongly recommended.

212111.overview:
Made in 1995, after releasing 'Keith's Quest' the same year on F1 Licenseware. Though complete, Trip 2: Trip War was never released until now.  It is a two-player only strategy-dogfighting hybrid.

You are daring pilots of lightning-fast Trip Ships in the year 2060, embroiled in a bitter war. Who will be victorious?

The aim is to shoot down your opponent, while collecting powerups to increase your speed, shot power and shield.

In War Mode, the players must also play a turn-based strategy game to aquire territory on the map, building and upgrading while sending your Trip Ships into combat.

212112.overview: A single player PD Tetris clone, referred to as a Sacred Geometry Puzzle, created n Blitz Basic by Tom Schoenlau in 1995 . This game contains a mode with extended shapes and also a level editor.

212113.overview: A one-player isometric shooter by NIVRIG Games with John Girvin doing the coding released just in time for the Christmas 2021 season. It is essentially a Christmas themed version of Turbo Tomato! Collect gifts and then give them to the children. Be quick, don't miss and avoid the Grunch! Build your multiplier for bonus points.

212122.overview:
A single player beat-em up game by developed and published by Sunteam, in 1992. There is a legend that states that during a time of great unrest, a child will be hatched from a great egg. This child will start his life free, with abilities beyond the understanding of men. The child shall be gifted with the power of goodness from the beginning, and will bring peace throughout the land.  
 
However, not all legends go according to plan... 
 
During the night the child was given to the world, a great battle between the dragon spirits of Good and Evil was taking place. Lightning lanced over the land and mountains crumbled to dust as the two ghostly figures fought for the possession of the baby. While the Good dragon spirit gave the enemy a fatal blow, the Evil dragon spirit swallowed up the egg and vanished.  
 
But a powerful monk found the tiny, bruised baby alive. Sensing the presence of evil all around the child, he enclosed him in many containment spells, slowing the child's growth to a virtual stop and then sealed the body into an airtight coffin and threw it into the seas. 
 
That was many, many years ago, and that is where our tale begins.

212217.overview: A galactic cross hairs space shooter. The view is from the bridge of your ship as you control the weapons systems to take out the enemy ships as they are coming right for you!

212248.overview:
A single player action/navigation game. Fly through the blocks in such a way that you can get the best speed and maneuverablity. Grab the jewels, avoid the reverse unless you really need to back for a goody or to reverse from a previous reverse or bouncy. Grab the extra lives, you'll need them. Watch the solid killer blocks and the gravity blocks will pull you down. Faster increases score, but is risky.  
 
Focus on the jewels, as getting them gets you to the next level.

212249.overview:
This AGA game is quite a find. It plays a lot like the arcade game Rodland. 

Coded by Paul Clarke and released by Lionheart in 1996.

212250.overview: A fantastic horizontal shooter, obviously influenced by Uridium. Shoot up a section of a giant alien dreadnought ship, when you've destroyed enough of it and the fighters they send out to fight you and you can move on to the next section.

212251.overview: A cute and fun Q-Bert clone game released in demo form in 1991 by Joerg Schmidt and Tarkus Team 91. The game has many features not featured in the original game, starting off much more difficult, in potentially requiring several color changes on all blocks, and having many baddies to avoid including springs, rubber balls, ghosts and other monsters as well as pickups that will help in game.

212252.overview: A martial arts fighting game from Savage Software released in 1993.

212253.overview: The aim of the game is simple.  Guide your ship through the various zones collecting power crystals and avoiding the aliens. Coloured passes will appear if you need them, enabling you to pass through the relevant force fields.

212254.overview:
A virus as infectious as a cold but as deadly as the plague swept this land, killing almost everyone. It is a mystery where the virus came from. As yet, there are no cures. You are the only survivor for miles. Survive! 
 
A game from Matt Briggs of Engine Nine Design.

212290.overview: A real Worms clone. Toadies are nasty little worms with a lot of nasty weapons. This is a game that supports up to 4 teams.

212360.overview: Talmino 2 is a Puzzle game, developed and published by Logistic Dreams, which was released in Europe in 1998. While this is a sequel to the original, it only has a single player mode.

212361.overview: Tank Attack from Culture is a multiplayer tank battle game for up to 6 players released in 1995. You start on an overhead view of the small singe-screen battle field, all tanks randomly placed and you must destroy all the other players or computer controlled tanks. This only takes a hit or two, things go VERY quickly.

212362.overview:
Tank Attack is a public domain game for up to four players.

Each player controls a round tank which they manoeuvre around a play area which has scattered obstacles that provide cover. Naturally, for a game with the word 'Tank' in its title, the player's vehicle is equipped with a big gun. The good news is that shells from the gun can be made to bounce off the walls and obstacles. The bad news is that the gun can overheat at which point it stops working so the player must run, hide and dodge until it cools down enough to work again.
The objective is to destroy the other player's tanks before being destroyed themselves.

Power-ups appear randomly throughout the levels however they all look the same so no-one has any idea whether they will be beneficial or useful.

The game is joystick or keyboard controlled. There is no single player vs the computer option.

212364.overview: A Sokoban type game written in assembler by Tim Schattkowsky and released in 1992. Features include 4 worlds with 10 levels each, new graphics and sounds in every world, 32 colors, 5 stereo sounds, smooth animation, an integrated editor, and a code for each level.

212365.overview: Side-view chopper combat! Fly 7 different attack helicopters with 5 configurable, realistic weapon systems against over 29 enemy and allied units in more than 80 missions. Big explosions and weather effects. All missions and random mission generation included with registration.

212366.overview:
Toobz is a puzzle game involving coloured spheres, which are variously red, blue, green and yellow. They are fired into a level from various starting points, along a selection of tubes (or 'toobz'), and the aim is to guide them into finishing points of the correct colour. This is done using various rotation points, which can be turned so as to redirect each ball. If it hits the end of the point (with it not set to recieve a ball) it goes straight back where it came from.

The levels also include machines which recieve a ball and change its colour, in accordance with a pre-defined sequence.

After each finishing point recieves a ball, its target colour changes at random, so be careful of setting it up to recieve multiple balls in one go.

Points are awarded based on how much time you have left after getting the required number of balls across. Time is lost for each ball of the wrong colour that reaches the end - running out of time costs you one of your 3 lives

212367.overview: A German language strategy trading game.

212368.overview: Trzech wesołych pielęgniarzy! is a simple bloody action game. As an ambulance driver the player must deliver wounded patient breaking by crowds of city citizens before the time runs out. To achieve the objective, the driver can drive through pedestrians and throw grenades toward the inhabitants of the blocks. Suitable destruction provides a time bonus. Reaching the hospital area ends the game.

212633.overview: A tactical combat game for one or two players and editor in the tradition of Act of War. You take control of a group of heavily armed mercenaries and guide them through hell... A mission editor will allow you to design your own favorite arena. Created by Jens Granseuer. Pick one of the 8 built-in combat missions like BG1 Babysitter where you must stop the rebels from capturing or destroying the Beta Gleny Orgital Station.

212634.overview:
A quick and dirty Tetris clone created by Jason Hildebrand In 12 August 1996. This version of Tetris has the following nifty features:

	- 5 two-player modes including collaborative, and competitive
	- configurable sound effects 
	- multitasks (OS-friendly)

212635.overview: An updated version of Tetrys (a Tetris clone) that was created by Lavialle Francois Denis of Crayon X and released in 1995

212636.overview: Based on the old Spectrum game Timebomb. Get the bombs, avoid the boots, get a high score! Timebomb is a simple arcade game (but thinking is very helpful). The player must diffuse six timebombs, before the time runs out. He can only move on blue squares (disappearing after single stepping - player can stuck with no any possibility of moves), and must avoid the skulls and boots. Each bomb a has time limit. The player has 3 lives - if he lost all lives, the game is over.

212637.overview: Push the toy boxes and candies across the floor to squash the bugs and other threats before they get you. You can blast the boxes if you need to, but it won't help your score. Press Q if stuck. If you take too long more baddies will show up.

212638.overview: A single screen shooter in the manner of Space Invaders, but with much better graphics. AGA Chipset required. Created by DJM and ToJa of DTA Software and released to shareware in February of 2000.

212639.overview: Dutch language draughts board game by Stef Keetman. The game is a draughts\checkers game played on a board with 10×10 squares, alternatively dark and light

212641.overview: Game that develops visual memory. Before you lay cards face down. Each card has a single identity. You can open any card. If the next open coincides with the previous one, they will remain open. This continues until all the cards will not open or will not leave you the time allotted. Match faces and parts of faces, primarily.

212665.overview:
Tronic is a little Breakout-clone with additional bells and whistles. Goal of the game is to use a racket, controlled by arrow keys or mouse, to hit balls that destroy bricks. When all the bricks for a level have been cleared, the player will advance to a next level.

The racket can fire rockets at any time by using a 'Gigablitz' weapon. To activate it, hold down the 'Alt'-key and wait for an indicator to reach the top. The trick is, in order to use Gigablitz, no balls must hit the racket, or the Gigablitz sequence will be aborted.

When some bricks are hit, they release gadgets that can be collected. Many of them enable more balls on screen, enlarge balls or let you advance to the next level. Beware though, do not collect red-coloured gadgets as they can shrink your racket, invert racket movement or substract points.

Finally Tronic also has a built-in level editor that lets you create, play and save your own Tronic levels.

212743.overview: Choose from several battlefields in this two player dueling tank game created by Robin Edwards and A. Murdoch and released as Licenseware in 1991. In this version the tank shots can bounce off walls for extra complexity and an element of surprise.

212744.overview: A tank shooter game created by Paul Ciulla, who has released both it and the source code in 1991. This isn't your average tank battle game, featuring original music, battlefields that make use of tanks, jets, rolling boulders, remote controlled gates and auxiliary canons and supplies. There are 13 different battlefields that are randomly selected. Setup screen for players to allow every game to be fully custom. Awards given for superior performance during the game.

212745.overview: Dynablaster\Bomberman clone made by Peter Bakota, Boris Ivic and Tibor Cxonkas of Tenax for up to four players. Tagged as being the ultimate multi player game.

212746.overview: This Tetris clone is for those of you with AGA machines only. Created in Blitz BASIC 2 he graphics are very good and so is the gameplay. There are a few extra features such as 2 player support, bombs and other things that drop down instead of the normal blocks. Enjoy! Created by Nigel Hughes and Mike Richards of FUNdamental Software.

212764.overview: Two guys with guns try to kill each other. A top down dueling game. Pick up bigger weapons and upgrades to shoot each other with. Includes 6 different maps. A medical drop will take you back to full health, a magazine will take you up to full for your *current* weapon. A dozen different weapons with varied amounts of default ammo, damage, blast, range and rounds\minute.

212765.overview:
TurboRaketti is a Finnish two-player "caveflyer", where you and a mate fly your Thrust-like ships around intricate levels with the ultimate aim of trying to shoot each other down. Each ship can be fitted with an extra weapon, which is triggered by pulling down on the joystick. The game has five levels to fight on:

    Ekolos is an ecologic level with earth tones and wild plantlife.
    Sitimus is an overhead map of a traffic system, a notion which doesn't quite fit in with how your ships have gravity to fight with.
    Metarola is a high-tech cave with pipe systems and industrial installations.
    Likvidius can be seen as the backyard of Metarola, since it is filled with chemicals and industrial waste.
    Tropulus is like the Finnish countryside, with red huts and pine trees.

Your "Turboranking" can be saved to disk for posteriority, and so that your friends may never forget who entered the first place in 1998.

212768.overview: Move all the counters from stack 1 to either stack 2 or stack 3. Only low numbers can be placed on high numbers.

212769.overview: A fake sequel to Tetrix, which was released to the scene in 1994 by Hawkeye Soft, who were notoriously lame for hacking other PD/shareware games that year (e.g. MEGABALL 3) and taking credit for work that wasn't their own. Rules are same as the original. It was released with the German Amigo Disk Magazine at one point.

212770.overview: Game created by Shaun Watters of Zamara Productions and released in 1994. To complete the level you must cover 95% of the grid with Tetris shapes. You can reject current blocks but this reduces your time. Eventually this idea would be recycled in a 1-4 player game and called Blokus that would be made into a incredibly popular board game.

212771.overview:
Earth is under siege from an alien threat. Huge genetically enhanced insects rampage across the planet. Man tries to fight back but hopes of success all but fade when their crack team is captured by the alien hordes. Desperate and out of time, a group of 10 men and women break away from their unit and form their own. Using vehicle remains from previous battles the group construct their own vehicles and weapons to counter attack the alien invaders in an attempt to crush their forces and strike at the heart of their very own home world. The unit was code named TANX.  
 

    Turn Based Strategy System
    10 Different Vehicles each with unique strengths and weaknesses.
    Upgrade with new weapons and shields!
    Large variety of weponry - Machine gun, shells, rockets, lasers and more!
    19 Missions, including assaults, acquisitions and clean sweeps
    Huge maps (3200 X 2560 pixels!)
    Engaging plot line
    Dozens of different sound effects
    Stunning Soundtrack
    Boss fights!
    Save Between and During Missions
    Battle against Commander Tyran and his unit of Cyberwolves. Your former unit.

212773.overview: A simple game where you have to guide your glider down to earth avoiding all the planes etc. and do it as quickly as possible without crashing. Game was distributed to Public Domain with full source code.

212775.overview: This version of Tetris Pro for the Amiga was created by Robert Ciesnik of Illusion Soft. It has additional features and rules including bombs that will fill holes in an area, $ pieces that give additional points, D deletes a line, plus or minus to change speed of play and so forth. A picture of the author is displayed behind areas cleared out, there are multiple images in the game pack shown on other levels including some that are adult in nature.

214317.overview: It comes to life! Guide our hero in to the Tomb of the Mummy in this creation to celebrate organizing the Cheltonian Geekfest by M. J. Nurney. Game created using backbone. Avoid monsters and traps, gather the keys and the ancient writings and other artifacts and make your way to the door to the next level. Pressure plates release items.

214359.overview:
A unique learning experience in reading comprehension.
Your child will be enchanted with the captivating stories of the Arabian Nights. The game includes three stories with stunning animated graphics:

Aladdin's Lamp
The Ebony Horse
Ali Baba

Each story has its own vocabulary building. The main learning objectives are to enhance your children's Reading Comprehension, Creative Writing and Language Arts Skills. The game contains over 600 multiple choice and fill-in reading and vocabulary questions.
Also included is a built-in word processor called TALE MAKER which enables your child to do creative writing, and a QUIZ MAKER authoring system to create their own questions and answers.
For extra value, there is a graphic ARABIAN MATCH GAME for developing memory and concentration skills.

214360.overview:
TeleGames is a collection of three classic board games to be played against a remote opponent via modem or null-modem. It can also be played taking turns at the same computer.

The games in question are chess, checkers and backgammon. The graphics are colourful, and can be seen both in 3-d from several perspectives as well as in a flat view from straight above. The package contains a phone book to keep track of remote opponents.

214361.overview:
TeleWar is a two-player strategy game intended to be played via modem, alternatively via null-modem or taking turns at a single computer.

In a split screen fashion, the top half of the screen features low resolution graphics, while the lower half contains a high-resolution user interface and a chatlog. The game is entirely controlled using the mouse, cycling between units of your army and pointing them at their destination, rotating turrets and firing using buttons at the bottom half of the screen.

The army consists of light and heavy artillery, light and heavy armour and supply trucks which can supply units with ammunition and fuel. Both supplies must be conserved, or your army will grind to a halt. Firing can be done in eight directions, requiring careful placement of your units. Each unit has different range, fire power and amount of fuel and ammunition. Since the screen is cramped, a single slow unit may block the advance of several others, necessitating careful movement. A turn may be sacrificed to call in air support, as long as the enemy hasn't destroyed your radio antenna.

The game is finished once the enemy army is destroyed, or if the flag is captured. Four scenarios and four kinds of terrain are supported.

TeleWar was followed by TeleWar II and had a medieval spinoff in the shape of TeleEpic. It was later refined into Operation Com•Bat.

214402.overview:
A Gambling game that uses three special Two Up dice.
The traditional game of Two Up was played with two old Australian Pennies. This version of Two Up uses three Two Up dice each having three heads and three tails. The dice version of Two Up is now played in Casinos World-Wide.

Features include:
• 3D Dice spinning on screen
• Bet on evens - 2 or 3 tails or 2 or 3 heads
• Bet on 6 to 1 - all tails or all heads
• Bet the whole bank
• Hall of fame recording the highest wins
• Hall of shame recording worst losses
• In-programme and printed instructions

214686.overview: A two-player head-to-head dueling shooter by RGBSoft.

214687.overview: Tanked Up is a one player game of tank combat. You are driving a rocket firing tank around in a maze-like arena. The arena is populated with computer controlled tanks hell-bent on destroying you. Your mission is either to destroy all the enemy or escape from the level. Shortly after the game begins, enemy tanks are added to the arena by means of teleportation devices, they will soon start to hunt you down. Every level has a maximum simultaneous number of tanks in the game at one time (this is set by the skill level). There is a finite number of tanks for each level based on skill setting, once you kill past this point no more tanks will be spawned. Each rocket impact causes 1 point of armor damage. Enemy tanks take four hits to destroy. You can drive through automatic doors and pick up rocket packs and armor boost to refresh your depleted supplies.

214688.overview: A two player public-domain tank duel shooter by Pink of Paradise Soft. Choose one or two players, choose level of difficulty and get to sniping! It will take several shots to fully disable your opponent.

214689.overview:
A multi-player party tank game from the author of HippoPlayer for 2 to 4 players. The game can be downloaded from Aminet Created by Kari-Pekka Koljonen, T. Lindström, and J. Päijänen of Hippopotamus Design in 1996. Tankkk does nothing more than turn your (once) powerful Amiga into an Atari 2600. Moving tanks around a monochrome screen will be a familiar first gaming memory to many so perhaps Tankkk taps into a node of gaming nostalgia. Up to five players can enter the maze and shoot at each other, making the game a must for gatherings. Although not recommended as a Christmas Day family pursuit it's perfect for beer drinking sessions with friends. There are a couple of different mazes and a number of settings to tweak the game.

The main reason why Tankkk is so good is that bullets bounce off walls. This seemingly simple feature expands the game's potential greatly since bullets can affect parts of the area away from the tank's immediate vicinity. Thus an arena with five players soon becomes extremely hectic.

214690.overview: This PD dueling tank shooter is a death-match without single player mode by Necropolis and released in early June 1994. Two or more tanks in a maze face off, you need at least one human opponent to play. Necropolis called this a game preview of a more fully featured game that was in the works, but perhaps never materialized.

214691.overview:
Inspired by the classic Tankz, this Blitz Basic game pits up to five human players in a battle tank-on-tank. The playfields are outfitted with some obstacles reminiscent to those used in a "snake" style game, offering protection from enemy fire. Bonuses pop up from time to time, though these bonuses may either increase or decrease your energy and firepower. As a result, apart from the usual "bomb your opponent to bits" method, one tactic in this game is to chase your opponent into harmful bonuses.

The game can be played in single matches or tournament style, where you may save your scores between rounds in order to resume later on.

214692.overview:
This is a Scorched Earth- And Artillery Duel-styled game for the Amiga. There are five weapons at the moment. The nice collapsing routine was done by Teijo Kinnunen, thanks!  When you play this game, please remember that this isn't even close to finished version. Maybe I'll put this to shareware
some day...

214693.overview:
A  four-player tank game created by Paul Atkin, Grant Young, Ben Campbell, Daniel Oaks. The game can be played by up to four people at a time - computer players hill fill in for any hissing human's, the aim of the game is to collect more flags than anyone else before the time limit expires, your vehicle can only carry three flags at a time so you must drop then back at your base before you can pick up more, Other players can attack you at any time and take the flags you here carrying or go to your base and steal them.  
 
There was both a playable demo and a full version of the game available via

214694.overview: A Tetris game for two players in cooperative mode from Jonathan Steven Horan of Trent Soft.

214695.overview: A shareware tennis game created by Christian Dreke and released in 1988.

214696.overview:
Teserae was first created on the Atari ST by The Albanian Sausage Corporation - a sort of game and a demo with great music and whizzy scrolling backgrounds. I remade a version for the Amiga in the early 1990's to help learn some of the machines features.

Guide the Tetris shapes to form neat lines with no gaps. Each time a line is completed it is removed from the screen and everything moves down. Complete several lines to proceed to the next, faster level. But you know how Tetris works, right?

214697.overview: Superb cricket strategy game at a stadium near you, right at your computer. Test Match Cricket is a sports and management game, developed and published by Challenge Software, which was released in Europe in 1994.

214698.overview: The program's primary purpose was copying disks, however most people remember this program because of the worthy Tetris clone added to the program to give you something to do while the formatting and nibble level copies took place. The application was released as part of the Assassins Disk Copiers disk set.

214699.overview: A Tetris written using Randyram Jam assembly course by Emiliano Esposito featuring up to 20 speed levels as on the Gameboy.

214701.overview: A two player, head to head version of Tetris created by Andromeda Software and released in 1988.

214702.overview: A  single player Tetris clone, created by Ross Fuller in AMOS as shareware and released in 1992. It was written to be more faithful to the original. Blocks dropped from a greater height score higher as are removing multiple lines, uses mouse controls.  The 1.0 version was released in April of 1992, with updates coming out until 1994.

214704.overview: A Tetris clone created by Gaz released in 1994 and released in the Assassins Ultimate Games compilation.

214705.overview: A Tetris clone created by Hayrettin Yildiz and released in 1994. Configure the specific width and height of the planning field, drop mode and game modes, even set up the music to play during your game.

214706.overview: Tetriz is, as the name implies, a typical Tetris clone, written as sharewar in AMOS Professional by Craig Burlock a hungry student in need of Amiga hardware and alternative music. It is level based, and every eliminated row counts up to the next level, as indicated by a bar in the score display, while a cheery tune plays in the background. Control is via joystick.

214707.overview: A one or two player shareware version of Tetris created by Peter Fregon in 1992. The game also supported Amiga to Amiga play through serial connection or modem. User changeable backgrounds, set starting levels, challenge modes. You can modify if next piece is shown, choose blocked blocks, "psychodelia", fast drop and statistics. You can also modify pieces and levels.

214708.overview: A version of a Tetris style game complete with a level editor, several difficulty modes and the ability to create music playlists. Released as a cover disk for Amiga Computing and on the Assassins Disk 021.

214709.overview: A puzzle game released on Assassins Disk 002. Think Ahead is a simple board game where two players battle in the fields of the mind. One of the players must be a human, but the other can be either human or computer. Player One makes horizontal moves and Player 2 makes vertical moves to gain as many points as possible. But it isn't always clever to get the biggest number so THINK AHEAD.

214710.overview: A shareware memory\matching game by Dirk Respondek and Thomas Schweppe of Zulu Softworx, there were multiple versions of this game with the most widely available version being 2.99.

214712.overview: A complex and constricting contest of combinations! The aim is to find out which balls are tied together. I found this game to be a bit too hard, even though I coded it myself. Every level gives a password, so you can pick up right where you left off.

214713.overview:
Tile Fall is a fun, simple, and very addictive game, in which you attempt to remove a number of coloured tiles from a grid.

Tiles can be removed providing that are touching another tile the same colour on at least one edge. Removing small groups of tiles (2 or 3 together) provide very small scores, but by removing other tiles, it is possible to get very large groups of tiles of a single colour. Removing these large groups results in drastically higher scores.

As tiles are removed, the surrounding tiles fall down to fill the spaces left. The game continues until no groups of 2 or more tiles are available.

214715.overview: A Gridtrap inspired game where you de-fuse time bombs before time runs out and they explode. You score points by reaching the bombs and disarming them, collecting bonus flags and clearing the bombs. You must avoid Skull & Crossbones, collapsing floors and a mean time limit that gets meaner as time goes by. Each level of the game consists of 10 grids which must be cleared of bombs before the time limit is up. Disarm bombs by moving the player on to the same square as the bomb. You collect flags in the same manner. Once you step on a piece of floor it will collapse and you cannot go back the way you came. So you need to plan your route carefully.

214718.overview: A commercially released ping pong game released on Schatztruhe #1223 and on the Spiele Special compilation.

214719.overview: Tittris from Richard Fhagher aka Dawnbringer is an early prototype of a game. Connect 5 of a shape or colour vertically or horizontally to remove those shapes.  However only horizontal lines count against the level line removal goal. Nicely presented, as you'd expect from Dawnbringer, and it soon gets tough as shapes drop faster and you lose if your planning to connect the colour or the shape.

214720.overview: A Bomberman style game for 4 usres created by S.C.R.O.T.U.M. and released in 1995.

214721.overview: A two player game based on a game by Magic Bytes called Blue Angel 69. The aim is to clean up a numbered field of stones. The level is that one player could only move and select stones horizontal, other vertical only. Very first one coded in Amos 1.3 and it seems to do nothing with the original one.

214722.overview:
A Jet Set Willy clone created by Tero Heikkinen and released in 1995. Top Hat Willy is an homage to the famous Jet Set Willy, a notoriously difficult flick-screen platform game with lots of screens. Guide Willy around his vast and very strange mansion, filled with death traps and dangerous creatures such as rolling razors, bunnyrabbits and flying TV sets, to collect his flashing items. A score panel on the bottom keeps track of how many of the many rooms Willy has explored and how many items have been picked up.

Even though THW makes some use of the Amiga's large colour palette, it remains true to its ZX Spectrum inspiration, so that each enemy is a single colour (or a single hue), dividing the screen in distinct 8x8 pixel blocks with separate colours for each block and having a black background.

214723.overview: A horizontally scrolling wave shooter with absolutely fantastic music from Nick the Greek and released to the public domain in 1994.

214724.overview: A single screen board game in the style of RISK, released by Paulo Laureano and Francisco Cordeiro and released as shareware in 1991.

214725.overview: An imaginative action game in which you must guide a ball-shaped craft through a succession of levels. These have a patchwork-quilt type display, with holes to avoid, and squares of various colors, which affect the craft's speed, both within its power potential and into warp, as well as a control-reverser and lots of holes. You can jump and thus avoid these holes, although you have a limited number of them for each level, and it's possible to adjust the speed through joystick or keyboard control. You also face a time limit on each of the levels, although your time is boosted every time you complete one.

214726.overview: An arena, some cover and a trusty tank for each of us. What fun we'll have! Based on Combat for the Atari VCS. The object is simple, destroy your opponent as quickly as possible. Only one shot per tank can be on the screen at one time. This can be modified in the setup, if desired. Game created by J. Lucas, M. Taylor and D. Vernon.

214727.overview: A puzzler by Hironymus Jumpshoe and DJ Braincrack.  Released 1993-06-11 on Amigo! issue 03/93.

214728.overview: A tabletop single-player card game from Markt & Technik in their Power-Disc magazine, specifically Power-Disc 6.

214729.overview: A two-player only 'Tron-Clone" that includes 4 different playing fields to choose from. The game was created by Manfred Linzner (Pink / Abyss) and released in 1995.

214730.overview:
This is a clone of a game known to all, it's Tron. This version was produced by a old hacker of the Amiga: Thierry Floquet. The game is simple: you're a pixel (if not a motorcycle) and you draw a line behind you in an arena. And It is thus necessary to "dual" longer than the opponent(s) in this arena to win. If you succeed, you pass at the next level. The difficulty is getting going on and we are rapidly in very arduous levels and with several enemies in the arena and full of obstacles.

Tronn remains very (perhaps too) classical, for example, music is missing during the game or multiplayer mode. But it can be a ton of fun to outsmart and outmaneuver the computer. Released as freeware by Thierry Floquet in 1998.

214731.overview: A licenseware maze game created by Trevor Taylor and released in 1991. The piece of software has been designed with a competition in mind. To reach the exit you must alter the maze by moving over switches which are circles of 1,2,4 or 6 colors. Each time you land on a switch, all the gates of the same color will move. In later levels some of the gates will take on false colors to make things more interesting.

214732.overview: An itty-bitty, tiny Tetris clone from Deadsoft published in 1991. This feels something like a joke game, but you decide if you have what it takes to go tiny.

214733.overview: Where the original tried to test the limits of the smallest playable Tetris game, this version flips that on it's head with an insanely large playscreen for very large tetrominos. Joke, or challenge...you be the judge.

214736.overview: An updated, two player version of PipeMania for the Amiga, created by Elmar Bransch of Digital Express and released in 1991.

214738.overview: Turbo Duel is a two player game based on the light cycles seen in the film TRON. This game has no AI element so there's no 'single player vs computer' option. The player(s) can customize the number of rounds per match, adjust the speed of the game, and toggle both music and the starfield background on/off

214739.overview: Turbo Invaders. PD Disk: G488 released in 1996 from Garfield Benjamin. The aliens all take more than one hit to take out, and avoid the red rain drops they give off as they will destroy you. Some special target drops give off powerups to increase your destructive potential. Clear off the current crop of aliens to move on to the next stage.

214740.overview: An AMOS based homebrew Arkanoid style game from Unlimited Design, released in 1997. Break the bricks, grab the falling powerups\powerdowns and figure out what each of the glyphs on them means so you can avoid the ones that make it harder to finish the level.
