214741.overview: Another puzzler from the puzzle sausagemaker, Harald Müller (Mueller). You have a certain amounts of spins that each numbered section can do, try to unite all the like colors to move to the next level.

214742.overview: A puzzle game from the ultra prolific Harald Müller (Mueller) released in 1994 and published by several companies in German and English.

214743.overview: The battle has now begun, but don't despair, because your cannon is unmatched, and with it you can drill another in the skull. - Finnish saying. "Another "Artillery"-clone... A bit like "Tanx", but simpler and slower and uglier. But in this game, both players can fire simultaneously. This game was my first "big" AMOS program (written originally in 1990, slightly improved recently), so it's slow and possibly bug-ridden." -Author's readme. Released in the PD compilation ASI-GAMES-VOL 131 from The Assassins.

214844.overview: A puzzle game created in 1991 by National Operators and also released in the classic compilation Spiele Special.  The captivating game with the black marble. Beware of falling, locked doors, etc. These brain twisters will warp your mind!

214873.overview: The third game in the series, following Kill Em All and Countdown to Extinction, it would be followed by Hangar 18. This adventure-shooter series is packed with 7 missions and tons of weapons. You are sick and are prepared for cryogenic sleep in 2025 as tensions between the superpowers is growing and Europe is uniting to throw the US off of European soil. You awake in Paris in the year 3655 in a time of heightened mental abilities but with the major cities in ruins from a great war between the superpowers and as resources became more limited. You are told the stories of the former wars and how your skills can help in their current battle, they need someone not sensitive to psychic attacks to fight for them and so you have been revived. Can you help them to finally achieve peace through superior use of firepower?

214947.overview: A well made side-by-side one or two player Tetris game, with statistics and multiple play modes from Digital, released in 1992.

214949.overview: A Sokoban clone with good music. A puzzle game in which you must push the balls into the slots using a logical approach.

215039.overview: A strategy game from Paul Huckstepp involving two colonies fighting over the same area of land. Released via Licenceware.

215040.overview: A vast strategy game involving colony creation and stabilization after the destruction of the Earth. Inspired by Utopia K240. Released via Licenceware by Paul Huckstepp as part of his Domination strategy series in 1996.

215049.overview: A version of Tetris made by Sky Devils with mature images in it to draw interest. Unsurprisingly this is a single player version of Tetris.

215107.overview: An unreleased Polish commercial 2D first person RPG\dungeon crawler style game released as a pre-release demo only from Insomnia in 1999.

215113.overview:
Tales from Heaven is a 3D varied-viewpoint platformer resembling things like Mario 64 and Pandemonium, with over 2000 polygons on screen at a time, and morphing and transparency effects. In Tales From Heaven you play as Zak, who must chase after his beloved cat, not only for his own benefit but also to retrieve a sacred talisman required to save a land above the clouds.

Your main weapon to progress through the 12 levels are a supply of bombs, of which more can be collected as you play. These have a 3-second delay and can hurt you if you don't retreat. Many creatures can be killed by jumping on their heads. To help performance on slower systems, lo-res graphics are available and the background graphics are optional.

215329.overview: An MS-DOS to Amiga conversion of the classic action shooter game Turrican II that supports AGA graphics. The second game in the Turrican series, which was originally developed by Factor 5 in the 90's and released on the Amiga, C64, CDTV, Atari ST, Amstrad CPC and ZX Spectrum, and later for DOS. While the game is basically the same as the Amiga version we know and love still to this day, it now features more colors and higher details throughout, improved controls for joypads, bug fixes and improvements, a new intro scene, more worlds to play through(still wip), as well as the choice of the updated PC sprite, or the original from the Amiga.

215381.overview: Tennis Champs is a 1995 Tennis Game from Mental Image, followed the same year by the game Super Tennis Champs. It was pre-released under the name of  Arcade Sports Tennis. Coded in AMOS by the excellently named Elton and Elliot Bird, manages to be better than all of them by taking its inspiration from the world of consoles and simply being a lot of fun. A clever and intuitive control system allows all manner of shots to be played with a one-button joystick. There are four different playing surfaces and a variety of players to choose from, and even a tournament mode.

215384.overview:
Thaurus is an adaptation of the Peg Solitaire board game. The game consists of two similar timed modes: Samotnik and Thaurus.

In Samotnik mode the action takes place on a standard board of 45 figures. All figures are the same and cover all fields except the middle one. The main task is to remove as many figures as possible, leaving only one at best. The pawns are removed by translating them in horizontal or vertical direction. The game ends when there is no possibility of movement. The result depends on the number of pawns remaining on the board.

Thaurus mode uses same rules but is much harder, as it introduces a special field (or fields) where the last remaining pawn (or pawns) should stay at the end. Before each new board player receives a level password.

215385.overview:
TAG is a 2-player shoot em up where you fly around a huge playing
field and blast your opponent! Simple, but very addictive!

215494.overview:
Help TIGER CLAW kick and punch his way through 24 screens of martial-arts mayhem to retrieve the four mystic scrolls before Fire Fist, Thunder Chain and Angry Tongue can reveal their true potential!

Fortunately, Master Lee has transferred some of the mystic scrolls’ power into four masks of endurance before they were stolen. Find these masks and use them wisely. As Confucius said: “He that would perfect his work must first sharpen his tools!”

TIGER CLAW is a relentless beat 'em up game developed by Lazycow and Saul Cross.

217250.overview: Tuesday is a game based on a series of non-existent graphic novels. In these novels, Gavin, the hero of the story, and his band of loser friends go on many adventures, which take them from comic shops to the mall, the sewers, a dinosaur park and beyond!

217254.overview: The aim of the game is to collect 20 pieces of candy (treats) before you collect 20 tricks (in this cane, spiders, ghosts, bats and skulls!). There is a strategy to winning this game, but I’m not going to share that with you. In this video tutorial I'll guide you through the entire process of creating this game, finishing with a great product. Full Source Code Included!

217255.overview: A clone of 'Artillery Duel' for up to eight players, including AI opponents.

217305.overview:
Based on the same engine as TeleWar, TeleEpic is a two-player medieval strategy game intended to be played via modem, alternatively via null-modem or taking turns at a single computer.

In a split screen fashion, the top half of the screen features scrolling low resolution graphics, while the lower half contains a high-resolution user interface and a chatlog. The game is entirely controlled using the mouse, cycling between your men and pointing them at their destination, choosing weapon and direction of attack using buttons at the bottom half of the screen.

Your army consists of a dozen men, all armed with throwing daggers, throwing axes, a bow and arrows and a sword for melée combat. Each man has a unique number of hit points and "stride" (movement points). In order to regenerate, he can be told to rest or heal for a turn. Battle may be done in eight directions, requiring careful placement of your units, and choosing a weapon with the correct range. Ranged weapons such as arrows or throwing axes can only be used while supplies last.

The game is finished once the enemy army is destroyed, or if the flag is captured. Three scenarios with different maps and terrain features are built-in. Games may be saved and replayed later, or transfered via modem to other users.

It was followed by TeleEpic II.

217306.overview:
TeleWar II is the sequel to the original TeleWar, a two-player strategy game intended to be played via modem, alternatively taking turns at a single computer.

Two armies (the blue one and the red one) confront each other on a scrolling battle field, controlled entirely by mouse. The basic game is the same as the predecessor, but with new terrains and scenarios and updates to the engine.

The game is finished once the enemy army is destroyed, if a player cedes the game, or if the flag is captured.

A follow-up, TeleWar III was announced but never published, but the game was further refined into Operation Com•Bat, which for the first time added artificial intelligence, making one-player games possible as well.

217327.overview: To the Rhine: The Allied Advance in the West is a strategy game, developed and published by Simulations Canada, which was released in 1988.

217422.overview: The Transcontinental Railroad is an Educational game, developed and published by MicroED, which was released in 1986.

217423.overview:
Triclops Invasion is an early 3D space combat game that was originally developed for the QNX operating system.

The solar system has bee invaded by the Triclops who parachute their giant walkers down to Earth. The only way to destroy a walker is to shoot off one of its three legs but as it has a cannon turret on its top the game's documentation suggests that destroying that first could be a good strategy. Once all five walkers and their satellite the game is won, if the Triclops destroy all three of the player's ships the Earth is lost.

The game also allows the player to record demo versions of the way they played the game and to turn off the enemy walkers so that they can just fly over the landscape.

The Amiga version was commercially released via mail order.

217429.overview:
Typing Tutor Plus Word Invaders is an Educational game, developed and published by Academy Software, which was released in Europe in 1986. 
THE MOST EFFECTIVE WAY TO LEARN TOUCH TYPING! 

Two great programs in one package. Learn to use your keyboard quickly and properly. TYPING TUTOR starts with the 'home keys' and automatically evaluates your typing performance, introducing you to new keys in many gradual steps as your skills develop. WORD INVADERS puts real excitement into your touch typing practice while rein- forcing proper typing techniques.

217534.overview: ANNOUNCING THE RELEASE AND IMMEDIATE AVAILABILITY OF TURBO SANTA DX22, an updated edition of the frantic arcade score-attack game for the Classic Amiga platform, based on 2021's hit game Turbo Tomato.

217544.overview: Part of the Telewar series (a.k.a TeleWar IV). Uses TeleWar engine. All known versions crash under emulation. This two-player only game is a strategy war game released in 1990.

217546.overview:
A Redpill Amiga conversion of an MSX game released in the late 1980's, like in the original version, the Franciscan monk Noni wants to join the Vitigudina order. To judge his valor, the order asks for a test of virtue: the monk has to collect weapons and use them to exorcise all the demons of a village.

Temptations is a Spanish flick-screen platform game. The game is divided in a series of levels, each with a series of screens. The player controls the monk's movements with the ARROW KEYS or the JOYSTICK. Pressing the SPACE BAR or the FIRE BUTTON shoots the projectile weapon he is carrying. The friar is killed if he touches the demons or some of the screen objects. His movement has inertia: after landing on a platform he usually keeps sliding forward (that is something that must be taken on account when planning how to move from one screen to the other). Shooting choice spots on the screen reveals hidden power-ups that can be collected, and some screens require the use of a specific power-up to reach their exit. The game starts with 10 lives and has no form of saving progress

219298.overview: Inspired by Tomcat Alley for the Sega/Mega CD, this game tries to offer full motion video sequences into this F14 Fighter game while you attack ground locations and have an occasional dogfight.

219379.overview: A scrolling platformer coded by Simon Hitchen with AMOS and published as licenseware in 1993.

411283.overview: Created by Coder : Curtis M. Wood, Graphician : Lisa K. Wood, Misc : Darin W. Anderson and James S. Diffendaffer and released in 1989 by Designing Minds in 1989, this read-along digital storybook tells the tale of the three bears.

417940.overview: Tenebra is an atmospheric puzzle game with rogue-like aesthetics. Guide the hapless protagonist to the exit. Poor guy is afraid of darkness and refuses to walk in the dark areas.

418040.overview: A single player brain game. Maneuver the falling letters in order to spell words horizontally and vertically to clear them and make way for more. A nice twist on Tetris.

418348.overview: A football\soccer game, the sequel to the original Track Suit Manager by Goliath Games. The game uses a revamped version of the original TRACK SUIT MANAGER artificial intelligence system written by Goliath coder and then-director, Doug Mathews.

418382.overview: A Frogger clone created in AMOS by Robert W. Benjamin with the standard freeway and water levels, with the addition of a rail yard to cross with fast moving trains a level with trucks and tanks and a slippery ice level.

418384.overview: This is a remake of Ork Attack. In this version, you defend castle Commodore against an endless stream of attackers with the Microsoft Windows 95 branding. Can't quite put my finger on it, but the background music was taken from another game.

418423.overview: An educational history title about the Titan disaster created by Paul Thompson and released as licenseware in 1995.

418441.overview:
Tracker Hero is a musical game for the Amiga that uses MOD song files. It can be played with keyboard, Joystick, Guitar or Dance Mat (Using Paul

Willingham's or PSX64 PS2 to Amiga adapter). Other PSX to Amiga CD32 adapters may also work. It has been developed on an Amiga 1200 and WinUAE using Amiblitz2, Personal Paint, Protracker and some other tools.  Additional songs can be downloaded from Aminet or from the game's page.

418561.overview: A shareware fruit machine\slot machine game written by Mental Image and published in 1994. It was released as part of the Bandit Mania compilation release. The game was also published in Amiga Action, 1994.

418659.overview: A text adventure with still pictures published by Coombe Valley in 1993. You must get your younger brother and sister ready and clean up the house so that mum will take you to the park.

418962.overview:
A single player shareware puzzler. What does a programmer do who can't think of anything right? Well, a pebble puzzle! And if he's really deep in the creative crisis, the 183rd "Tetris" variant will come out of it...
Ergo, we are again presented with the well-known blocks, but this time they appear in the middle of the screen and have to be puzzled together under time pressure to form single-color squares, which then disappear from the screen. The joystick or fire button is used to push and rotate, and the space bar is used to place them. If you get the right number of points, you get the password for the next level, where things get a bit more difficult due to the different shape and size of the "building site". The principle of the game means that more and more leftover bricks" reduce the area that can be built on, and of course blocks of the shape and color that you would need right now never appear, in short, the "Tetris". usual hustle and bustle breaks out. In this respect, the game has a certain addictive quality that you cannot deny.

419044.overview: This is a turn-based strategy game board game card game, now with more monsters, more power-ups, more strategy. This is the 7th game in the Total Chaos series.  This is the direct sequel to Total Chaos 6:  The Newbie Edition.

419729.overview:
This is a direct sequel to my popular game Tenebra, with many exciting new game play elements, including a portal gun!
Similar to its prequel, Tenebra 2 is an atmospheric puzzle game with rogue-like aesthetics. . Guide the hapless protagonist to the exit. Poor guy is afraid of darkness and refuses to walk in the dark areas.
Tenebra 2 contains 35 levels and works on both PAL and NTSC machines.

420574.overview:
A remake of the famous Tankkk, renamed to TankX and updated (after 27 years). This new version has been updated after a slight *cough* delay. It is now called TankX, and supports 7 simultaneous players (up from 4). Many other improvements have been made as well. This version was developed in co-operation with the https://www.amigalive.com discord-community, who provided improvements ideas, testing, new battlefields and in-game music. Cheers!

The original version was called Tankkk, where the number of k-letters denoted the amount of tanks in the game. This one should then be called Tankkkkkkk, but that would be silly. So up to 7 simultaneous players possible!   - Tank #5 with a third set of keys which default to: U, T, 6, Y, F.
  - Tanks #6 and #7 with a parallel port joystick adapter.


Check out AmigaLive for some TankX online mayhem!

420579.overview: Another Jeff Minter psychedelic creation, a light synthesizer for your Amiga. Change the phase, the offset, colors and influence the lights with your Amiga mouse for a trip to the dark side of your monitor. Converted to the Amiga by Andy Fowler.

420720.overview: A game featuring monochrome graphics (marmite for some!), but also deadly enemies such as bats and snakes, charming animations, nasty spike traps, and a nod to classic monochrome platformers games many of us still love to this day. The game is a tribute to Tony Halik.

420921.overview:
This is an early DEMO of Tempest2000 for the Amiga, written by Elton Bird of Mental Software.
Best played on a 28MHz or more A1200 with Fastmem. Lower spec. turn the fill OFF.
I'm kind of stuck with what to do with it! If you have any interest in perhaps buying a finished version for a coverdisk, I'd be happy to hear any offers.  Obviously the fact that it's an Atari game that's now out on PC and imminent on PSX/Saturn
may be a problem for anything other than a PD release, but I think it's a little bit above being PD.  Love to hear any feedback/suggestions. If you can, give me a ring and let me know what you think of it.

420929.overview: Two versions of this game can be played, the demo version or with the Shareware code you can play the full version of the game created and published by MIA Software in 1989.

420932.overview: Remember Frogger? Did you ever wonder what it would have been like to be driving one of the cars going back and forth on the road?

420934.overview: An AMOS platform game by Emmanuel Icart of Momor Productions in 1996. The game is kind of like a cross between Lode Runner married with Flashback. A level editor was included. 20 levels were included, with some others to be found.

420949.overview: THUNDERHELL is a one level demo of a horizontally scrolling space shooter created by Paolo Cattani in 1990.

421155.overview:
A German language fantasy, illustrated text adventure game made by Achim Kern and published by OASE in 1993. In the game you are Taran and you have to defeat the dark forces and help your king to regain his kingdom. More than 20 years later, developer did enhanced ports to AmigaOS 3, AmigaOS4 and other platforms. Taran is a knight in a fantasy kingdom who gets tasked by the king to find his lost insignia of power, his crown and sceptre. If Taran succeeds, he will get to marry the king's beautiful daughter and will have half of the kingdom for his rule.

The game plays like a classical text-adventure, but it has some graphical menus for convenience. Four standard commands and movements can be chosen from an interface. Choosing "examine" will give a list of all objects you can examine in the room. You can also use cursor keys for movements and the function keys for certain commands. The game has a hunger/thirst mechanic, so you need to eat and drink on a regular basis. Your inventory is limited to ten objects.

421257.overview: Return through the snow to the research facility, but you must fight your way through the infected humans and alien dogs.

421332.overview: An unofficial Scorpion Engine Demo created by Acidbottle in 2023. In it you pilot an attack chopper and take out all the foes that pop up in front of you. Get them quick before they take you out. Unfortunately only the first few baddies exist in this demo, but you can finish it off any way you want to.

421422.overview: A game from Wicked Software's 50 Great Games release in 1990. A 3D game that really takes the name to heart as it can be used with Red/Blue 3D glasses! Bounce the ball off paddle to hit as many tiles as possible with the 5 balls/lives you've been given. Use the Amiga mouse to move the paddle around the floor. Use the left mouse to launch any new balls. But don't click the left button during the game or it will end your turn. Later, in 2018 this was released to public domain.

422250.overview:
In Tolteka you must Help Prof. Dr. mad. Tony Style! Ancient cultures are the hobby of the slightly absent-minded scientist. And sometimes he is even successful in his excavations - like with Tolteka, the underground city labyrinth that he wants to explore with remote-controlled robots. But our old professor is an excellent archaeologist, but he knows nothing about technology. Accompany Prof. Dr. Style to the remains of ancient civilization. Discover a new world of strategy gaming in the city labyrinths of Tolteka...
• 3fach splitter Screen
• 1 and 2 player option
• bidirektionales Scrolling
• lots of moving sprites
• 38 Level
• 60 different image elements
• Highscoreliste
• 10 different opponents

422313.overview: A S.E.U.C.K shareware game by Loz in 1994. A sequel to this shooter called Tech War Mania Mode was released later the same year. You form part of a secret task force known as united freedom undercover operations in technology, code named Necoth, The latest project RAD is just under completion. The laser recharge isn't quite perfected yet but will charge on certain targets. INTRUDER ALERT! All defenses breached. All exits are blocked by the aliens the only way out is to fight your way through.

422319.overview: An AMOS based freeware text adventure written by Jason Strudwick in 1994. An accident in of the GSC Time-Laps where an uncontrolled distortion has caught up an energy crystal in a temporal rift. You will need to travel through the rift, repair the crystal to use to power a return trip and close the rift!

422322.overview:
An AMOS based freeware game by Paul Jenkinson from 1992. Long ago, two opposing valleys joined forces to defeat a band of Orcs threatening each individual valley. Before the final battle the two rulers met and brought together the great treasures of each valley.

One valley produced a beautiful solid gold chain.The other valley brought forth a pure diamond of immense value. The two items were joined to produce a extremely beautiful and valuable talisman. It was hidden in a place only known to three fighters from each valley. If the battle was won, the talisman would be paraded and both valleys would become one. During the battle all six fighters lost their lives and the talisman was lost forever.

It is your turn to seek fortune and glory, and saying your last farewell you head off into the unknown. Traveling through forests, towns, caves and swamps you come across a small Orc camp. Three small Orcs sit by a glowing fire eating the remains of some animal. Being small you think them easy gain and draw your sword for battle. Hiding in the shadows were five other, bigger Orcs. Knocking you out, they carried you for four days as reserve food. On the forth day they became tired of hauling you around and hid you in a small cave, to call back at a later date when you became a little more decomposed and tasty.

On the fifth day you wake, tired, hungry, weak and with a hell of a headache. Crawling around you find a small puddle of water, formed by droplets of water from the roof above. Drinking the water causes a strange sensation, a warm feeling overcomes you and as you drink more, all ills are mended. You have heard of such healing springs from the bards, but have never met anyone who actually drank from one. Back to full health you decide to continue your quest...The Talisman* is a freeware adventure with RPG elements for the Amiga. The interface is entirely mouse-driven, and slightly resembles the one used on the Legend text adventures. At the top-left of the screen there is a non-interactive picture, and besides that a series of buttons with verbs:

422337.overview: A text and picture based adventure game created by Sceptre Soft and released as shareware in 1993.

422340.overview: A platform game. Collect hearts and locate the hidden switch before finishing the level. A PD game from Gunter Meister in 1992. There once was the land of Tortiga, That's where the Nassars lived. Their chief was called Tonga. Now it happened that the sorcerer Orrara kidnapped Tonga's bride and held her prisoner in a secret dungeon. Tonga must try to find the dungeon. He has to face many dangers. He has to pick up objects that are hanging in the air on his way. There are secret switches that allow you to progress. Dangerous monsters cross his path that he has to avoid. Invisible traps complicate his journey.

422341.overview: A space shoot-em-up dueling game for 2 players released as freeware by Paul Hamilton in 1993. It was inspired by Biplanes, Thrust and Virus. The first player to 25 points wins.

422346.overview: An Amigo! coverdisk in 1992, this puzzle game for one or two players from Ingo Frick, Christian Reismüller and Oliver Wierich was released 1992-06-05 on Amigo! issue 03/92.

422361.overview: Choose your weapon and shoot a variety of pop up targets in this shareware game by Ian Chisholm. released in 1996.

422408.overview: A freeware text adventure game created by Tony Heap of Heyley Software in 1991 using the Hatrack II adventure game generator. The game was included on the Amiga Computing issue 37 (June 1991) coverdisk. Pit your wits against some cunning problems in this Treasure Island text adventure.

422419.overview: A small version of Tetris you can play from your workbench desktop. It was created by Edgar Vigdal and released to PD in 1991.

422422.overview: An AmigaBASIC game programmed by Ma We Crew and released as freeware in 1988. It is a German language trucking management company game. Trucking is a trading and business simulation for 1 - 5 players. The number of game participants is asked at the beginning, as well as their names and company names, since each player runs his own company as a freight forwarder. For each new game, the company was founded in January 1988. At the end of each year, the points achieved by the players are compared with the YUPPI list and an entry is made if necessary. Every player begins their entrepreneurial career with the same starting capital; only the available overdraft facility changes from player to player. A game for many exciting hours...

422468.overview: A game similar to Boulderdash, but simplified for a younger audience created with the Emerald Mine Editor. Hurry! The darkness approaches. The forces of evil awaken. Hungry for mortal souls. You must be gone from here. The evil of chaos is strong and you ....mortal....are weak.

422480.overview: A freeware racing, avoid-it game created by Matthew Goode and released in 1994. This game can't be completed. Just survive as long as possible to get a high score.

422481.overview:
You had a argument with your girlfriend, she ran into the tunnel. Do you dare to follow her? 
 
A horror/jumpscare game written in AmiBlitz3 by 8080 aka Sami Vehmaa.

422508.overview: A Linear Action Adventure for the Commodore Amiga

422513.overview: An example game bundled with Easy AMOS, published by Europress Software in 1992. A top down, multi-directional sports game for one or two players. The single player game has two different AI levels so you can start off easily and get used to the game in progression before playing two player side by side competition mode.  It appears to be modeled after Anco's Kick Off game.

422514.overview: An AMOS based, 2 player competitive racing game from François Lionet that was published by Europress Software in 1992 as an example game of the Easy AMOS system pack.

422565.overview: A Polish language educational driving quiz\test developed and published by Atares in 1994.

422768.overview: An unreleased Polish game from Logical in 1998. adventure and trading game with a pinch of RPG elements and tactical elements (fighting on a chessboard). The game takes place at an unspecified time on a planet inhabited by the Pel tribe. These are the indigenous people of this planet and the player takes on the role of one of the natives. Pelovians are not very technically advanced, the ambitions of most of them do not reach further than their own backyard, but there are exceptions who dare to dream of traveling to all parts of the planet. Such Pełs most often become traders or disappear without a trace. The character controlled by the player is the grandson of one of the traders, who leaves him an intriguing letter with some cash so that he can escape from his backwater. By going from city to city (village, capital, mine, desert), finding various more or less interesting things and encountering various adventures along the way (attacks of robbers or wild animals, the player gains experience and money. He also gains recognition and respect, and being a respected citizen he can join the guild. If all goes well, over time you might even get into the royal court. During your escapades in pubs or listening to the whispers of royal chambers, he sometimes learns about visitors from other planets.

422808.overview: An AMOS based Licenseware game created by Frank Oliver in 1997. Time Warrior is a deep adventure where you came from the future to change the history of mankind.

422879.overview: The first in the series of 10 Trek Trivia shareware games and question sets from Micro FX Software that all released in 1988. This game had a larger focus on the original series but embraced all things Trekkie.

423039.overview:
A puzzle game created in ABasiC by David Addison in 1986. Back in 1985, the first Amiga 1000 computers came with the ABasiC programming
language by Metacomco. Unfortunately ABasiC does not work under Kickstart 2.0 (V36) and later, but can be patched to fix the problem. Apart from historical interest, David Addison wrote some excellent games in ABasiC. The David Addison games originally appeared on Fred Fish disks, like this on disk 36. In it you use cursor keys to select and alter desired values. Press the function keys for some build in waveforms. F10 toggles between white and colored dots. You can also enjoy the 3D maze represented in 2D.

423046.overview: TERROR LINER II is an adult "freeware" version of the game TERROR LINER puzzle game (hacked by Vision One for Alpha Flight), which was commercially released a year earlier in 1989 by Wolf Software. It is a Qix style game, wall off the sections of the picture and see the pixelated skin.

423160.overview: A shareware Pipeworks style AMOS game created and published by Chris Hodges in 1995.

423165.overview: A CLR Licenseware game by Sparx in 1990. A jigsaw type program for young children. There is a choice of 24 puzzles on the disk with two difficulty levels. The easy level gives a grid into which the puzzle pieces are placed, the hard level just gives a black tray with no helping grid. Once the puzzle is created you will be shown how long you took.

423172.overview: Released as version 3.0 of the beta, this Tetris inspired puzzle game by Studio V98 came out in 1994 and included the source code for the game. It included four modes of play: Enduro, Challenge, Vs Match and Theory.

423173.overview: Pixel Precision Presents Tile Trial, a timed shareware sliding puzzle game. You have three minutes to complete each puzzle. The game ends when you fail to complete a puzzle. After each puzzle, you will be awarded points according to the time taken to complete the puzzle, number of moves taken and the difficulty of the puzzle.

423176.overview: A four player, freeware tank shooter from Grid North in 1997.

423177.overview: You have laid your hands on a copy of the game TECHNO TRON, from the Swedish studios of Alive Software in 1991. The object of the game is to run the other players into the walls or the line that is drawn behind the vehicle. A two player only game. There are 25 levels of play.

423179.overview: A two player, freeware pong style game by the Swedish, Division A, dropped in November 1992. Unsurprisingly the game is backed by techno music.

423180.overview: Based on the board game of the same name, this shareware game by Markus Riehl and published by Lizard Soft in 1992.  The game is based on the 1934 novel Murder on the Orient Express by Agatha Christie.

423218.overview: A two player Tron style Worm\Snake game created by Thomas Jansen and released as public domain in 1990. Based on the Tron Light-Cycle-Races from the immensely successful Film.

423266.overview: Turbo Hockey was a shareware hockey game for two players made over a single weekend and released as shareware in 1993. A four player sequel would be released the next year.

423269.overview: An educational licenseware game created by Harry Collier and published in 1997. True history begins with the reign of Henry VIII. the civil war swept from the land, the relics of the Feudal System, and a new and better order of things arose. During the Tudor Period was seen the dawn of commerce, literature and the breaking of the yoke of the Roman Catholic church. These were times when an Englishman was proud to be called so...

423287.overview: A one or two player Tron Lightcycles\Worm\Snake game with anime style graphics and voice samples from Sunteam and released as freeware in 1992. The bloody, explosions when you crash give the game a satisfying ending every time.

423288.overview: A Tron style Worm\Snake game for one or two human players and up to 6 additional CPU based players created as PD freeware by Dynatron in 1992.

423289.overview:
A single player, freeware, graphical train track management game from Electrosoft in 1995. In this game, you have to direct colored trains into stations of the same color by switching points on the track. The trains are red, blue or yellow. To change a point, move the cross-hair over the point using the mouse and press the left mouse button (LMB). During the game, holding down the space bar will speed up the trains. pressing 'P' will pause/unpause the game and pressing, Escape (Esc) quits the current game. The Jolly Good sample can be toggled with the 'S' key if it gets on your nerves! The 'T' key can be used to force the release of another train from a station. 

Trains are released from stations randomly, with up to four running at any one time. When a train is released, a whistle sounds and the guard at the top of the screen holds up a flag whose color matches that of the station from which the train is leaving.

423300.overview: An AMOS based, freeware life simulation game by Fly By Nite in 1993. It attempts to give you an updated version of the Eliza game where you chat with the computer about what is bothering you and the computer guides you towards greater introspection.

423336.overview:
The Task: An exciting space adventure awaits you here. An out-of-control spaceship. You are were sent out to avert the threat of explosion on the cruiser and to make the ship safe again. To recover, you rely primarily on your ability to combine things. Because there are so many items that
must be found and so many puzzles that must be solved. Since the artificial gravity has failed, you are forced to maneuver with your jet pack, which has a simple keyboard operation. Unfortunately, real-time polygon graphics have their price, because the game only runs on Turbo Amigas (68020 or better). A freeware game by Lipowski Bobe, from 1995.

423337.overview: A shareware Snake\Worm game created as freeware by Vaughan Roberts in 1995. It has configurable speed, sounds and obstacles.

423347.overview: A timed freeware collect'em up game released in 1990. The game even came with a level editor to make and trade your own levels with friends.

423349.overview: A Lunar Lander style action game created in Blitz BASIC by Christian Steiner in 1998. Unlike many lander style games with generated rather than static landscapes, this one has additional obstacles to avoid such as meteorites and UFOs.

423377.overview: A 3D Construction Set based adventure, created by Bruno Pommier and released as shareware in 1992.

423383.overview: A single player, SEUCK based shooter released as Licenseware by Gary Swann in 1991. This shooter, inspired by the Top Gun movie has you blasting MIGs and dodging missiles, flying over the high seas.

423386.overview: Top Of The League a football\soccer management game and was ported by the original author from the Amstrad CPC title of the same name and published by Scogen in 1992.

423387.overview: A one or two player puzzle game created and published by Backwoods Software and Computational Software in 1989.

423389.overview:
A one or two player board game created by Spence Davies and released by Deja Vu Software in 1990. Touchstones is played on a 12 x 8 board using 72 'Stones'. Take turns to place Stones next to ones of same shape or color or both. (diagonally does not count). Stones placed around the edge of the board do not score and are of strategic importance only. The next stone to be placed is at the top of the stack on the right of the screen.
Scoring:
A 1 sided match A 2 sided match scores 1 pt scores 2 pts
A 3 sided match scores 4 pts
A 4 sided match scores 8 pts

423406.overview: Make your way carefully through the Temple of Elemental Evil in this text adventure homebrew version by Genasoft in 1989.

423539.overview: Fire up your lightcycle and take out your opposition, wind and swerve and block them off when you can. A game based on the cycle competition from the Tron movie and made by Darius Hardy in 1995.

423600.overview: The story of this homebrew, Czech language text game is quite simple, the player becomes Radomír Danenberger for a moment, whose goal is to become a programmer in the world-famous software company Toayen.

423621.overview: The Tipster By Sidemouth Software 1990 Horse Racing Prediction Program. Tested and working on an Amiga 600, sold in two versions, a mail order version presented as a folio and a plastic clamshell version for storefront sales.

423677.overview:
Tygard is a game in which you have to collect pairs of hats on the heads of the men waiting below so that as many of the same ones as possible are stacked on top of each other. When you have collected six of a kind, they disappear and the gentlemen breathe a sigh of relief. Here too you have extras like the fireball, um...to burn away annoying hats. You can also play Tygard with two people at the same time to compete. The background music ensures that you quickly forget your surroundings and devote yourself fully to the game.

Published individually and as part of the Intelligent Fun game pack with Cubic.

423679.overview: Peg Puzzle aka Towers was Created by James as freeware in 1990 using ASM 68k. It is a basic Towers of Hanoi puzzle game where the object is to move a pyramid of colored disks from the left peg to one of the other pegs. You may only move one disk at a time, and you may not place a lager piece on top of a smaller one.

423695.overview: An unfinished PD platform game roughly in the form of a Turrican-like fighter who can blast and jump over the ghostly baddies in front of him.

423726.overview: A two player action game, catch the tots tumbling out of the burning building, but beware as the tots will tumble out of the life net and you may have to bounce it twice into the ambulance. To make things more interesting once one baby bounces out of the inferno they all come tumbling down, you should be able to juggle them all in the air if you are fast and crafty. A freeware PD game from David Ashley in 1988.

423828.overview: A Polish educational game focused on math published by Techland Soft in 1994.

423890.overview: A quick game of Theme Park Xmas on the Amiga. This was released by CU Amiga magazine in December 1994. Xmas puddings, Christmas trees, Santas, grottos and of course snow is all featured in this one-off special! Like the original, dominating the exciting world of Theme Park ownership is your goal in this strategy game from Bullfrog. The first task is to set up your rides within the available land, structuring convenient paths and queues and ideally leaving some space for bigger rides once they become available, and include some lakes and trees to increase the park's allure. Rides range from Teacups and Haunted Houses to the biggest most elaborate roller-coaster you can design, and water rides that loop around other rides.

423894.overview: A single player, freeware puzzle game created by Marcin Oriowski and only related to the big game franchise as there was a puzzle in the Lara Croft game that served as an inspiration for this game's puzzle. Seen here from an overhead view instead of the first person view in that game.

423993.overview: SunMaze on Aminet brought 3D FPS Look and Walk to Amiga in 1989. This is a 3D Maze FPS game by Werner Gunther where you can walk around in the different kind of mazes with the numeric keys on your Amiga keyboard. You walk forward with the 8 key and turn either left or right with 4 or 6.

424369.overview:
A Polish language educational game by Twin Spark Soft in 1994. Pythagoras is the first comprehensive program for learning mathematics. The emphasis in the program is on learning the methodology of solving tasks applicable at subsequent stages of learning. The program can assess a student's results and diagnose his or her achievements. Based on Pythagoras, you can find out your shortcomings in understanding the material in a very clear way. 

Pythagoras has a number of mechanisms that make it impossible to "cheat" the assessment of knowledge of the taught material, which allows this program to be treated as the cheapest but demanding tutor. The professionalism and substantive correctness of the theoretical materials contained in Pythagoras are guaranteed by the authority of their author, a doctor of mathematics from the Jagiellonian University.
During the learning phase, the program asks additional guiding questions and explains the next stages of solving the tasks. You can gradually give up on this help, because the end goal is to solve tasks on your own. Tasks can often be solved in many ways. The tips suggest a method that minimizes the chance of making a mistake. The complete course consists of the following parts (sold as separate programs):
7th and 8th grades of primary school and secondary school exam,
grades 1 and 2 of secondary school.
grades 3 and 4 of secondary school.
Pythagoras is the cheapest tutor!

424371.overview: A Polish language educational driving quiz\test developed and published by Atares in 1994. Version 2 of the quiz would be released at the end of the same year.

424418.overview:
After crashing your plane at sea, you end up drifting to a small island, with not much to survive. You explore, and find out the island was inhabited, years ago. But why did the people leave? And why is there a fence around the white house at the top of the hill?

TRISTAM ISLAND is a text adventure made from the mold of Infocom; expect a large geography to explore, lots of prose, a rich parser, diverse puzzles, some humor and some darkness. To use Infocom's classification, I'd rate the game's difficulty as "Standard"; however, the game's design is modern and eschews all the frustrations commonly associated with 1980s text adventures. No hunger timers, no frustrating mazes, no blocking situations that force you to restart!

425395.overview: An unofficial port of the Tengen version of Tetris for the Amiga 1200.

446335.overview: A sequel to Trapped 2, based on a revised and corrected version of the Trapped 2 engine. This new marvel will be called Fratzen Geballer and will implement new and spectacular effects such as mipmapping. lensflares, dithering and very atmospheric lighting effects. Everything will be set in a space station. The game would remain unreleased, with this demo dropped in 1997.

447155.overview:
A highly customizable Italian language Casino game for one player and up to 3 computer opponents created by Giovanni Iacobelli. Tressette a Perdere is a popular Italian card game. In this digital version the player will play against the PC's artificial intelligence that will split into three opponents. The game ends when one of the players reaches 51 points and 
it is won by the player who scores the fewest points.

448201.overview: A homebrew casino game where you play in Dobbs Casino, created by Steve Treatment and released in 1993.

449309.overview:
The first pack, from the School Software line, is a mini-adventure called "The Three Bears." Inspired by numerous fairy tales, including "Goldilocks and the Three Bears," the authors have created a simple graphic adventure set in a mythical world populated by talking cats, wizards, wicked witches and dark dungeons. This graphic adventure aims to rescue three bear cubs from the clutches of the wicked witch who captured them after they got lost in the forest.

A map shows you where you are and where you can go. As you progress, you encounter friends and foes who offer help or ask for things. Progress in the game depends on completing certain tasks in a specific order. For example, if you don't pick up the key when you find it, you won't be able to open an important door elsewhere, which will hinder any progress.

This type of gameplay strategy is beneficial for children's development. an understanding of sequence and logic and encourages forward planning.

449323.overview:
A small, sneaky strategy game! Following templates, you have to click on certain patterns in color. Of course, with a time limit and some nasty tricks!
 
Published in the Amiga Spielesammlung Band 2 compilation.

449695.overview:
A game in the style of Tempest with simulated vector graphics. In the game you use your mouse to move your ship around the line structure, left mouse to fire. Right mouse will drop a "shadow". You advance in levels by killing the number of bad guys indicated by ships on the top of the display. If enemy sparks make it to the top you will die.

Published in the June 1992 Amiga Resource Disk accompanying the Amiga edition of Compute Magazine.

449699.overview:
The TWON game is a 1994 freeware game by Soren Staun-Pedersen.

The game basically looks and plays like a Tron Light Cycles game, but set in space.

450118.overview: Tronic is  a Tron Light Cycles variant for up to 4 players. It was developed by Unrelated Dimension and released into the public domain in 1995.

450224.overview: Treasure Search is a public domain adventure game developed by Peter Hickman and released in 1990.

451893.overview: An electric (toy) train construction set game simulation. Published as shareware, binary only, source available from author, who is Dennis Saunders and he made this in 1990. Build your track, choose your cars and test the circuit and switches you've created.

452051.overview: An unofficial remake of the game TOWER OF EVIL from the C16, plus4, c64,Z80 to Amiga

452499.overview:
Tale of Evil is an unofficial sequel of "Tower Of Evil" for the Commodore Amiga.

The Story:
Once upon a time there was a little girl, her name was Olivia. Like all strange children, Olivia loved to play in the nearby cemetery. It was here that she met the witch's cat Schrodinger, who went to the cemetery not to play, but to collect magic components as the witch's assistant. As days passed, the witch watched the forming friendship with more and more jealously. One day, she came to a terrible decision. She decided to put them both six feet, under the ground. Since the witch was not Schrodinger's first owner, he already had experience with mad scientists and poison capsules, so he managed to avoid his death, but sadly the little girl had no luck. Like all cats, Schrodinger moved easy between the world of the living and the dead. As a guardian of the underworld, he decided to bring Olivia back to the world of the living by collecting the little girl's remains and memories, and if only in the form of a ghost, they would take revenge on the witch together.

Gameplay:
There are eight different terrains, each divided into 9 sections. The goal is to collect all the items on the map with Schrodinger (the cat), who cannot defend himself on his own. There are 6 objects in each area, when you have all 6 objects, you can go to the next through the portal (pentagram). Olivia comes to life by collecting the first 6 items. You can switch her to follow or stop with the fire button. She is not only able to shoot back at enemy creatures, but earthly projectiles don't affect her either, so Schrodinger can even hide behind her if necessary. She always attacks the closest monster to you. In case of injury, he can heal by catching the mice. They can get to the witch if they have already collected all 48 items. The witch can summon monsters, and even Olivia can't neutralize her magical fire, so we can't hide behind her. 
Crystal balls are only part of the story.
Olivia can be controlled by a second player if she is already 'alive'. You can take control of her by pressing the fire button on the second joy port.

Since the game did not prove to be easy, a level-code system was subsequently built in. The code is made up of a sequence of 3 symbols, which can be entered in the menu using the joystick. If the code is correct, we hear a cat's meow and the cat's eyes turn green. During the game, the codes are displayed in the magic sphere associated with the given area.

452516.overview: Tic Tac Toe Warrior is a 1-2 player co-operative shoot em up developed by Chris Geist using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit. It was released into the public domain in 1994.

455554.overview:
There was an earthquake in the Kilimanjaro Mountains in Africa. As a result, a huge cave was exposed. Researchers were sent there to check what was inside. Only one man returned, who told terrible things about huge dungeons full of dangerous robots. Some of the researchers could still be there. It was decided to send a tank there to explore the dungeons and destroy the aliens. You will command this tank - good luck!

Info:

There are 15 levels ahead of you. Every second one is randomly generated. Save your ammo. You can replenish it by collecting ammo in dungeons. You can also collect additional armor that will protect your tank from one hit. Watch out for the bombs lying around. You will get bonus points for collecting the missing researchers.

456116.overview: A wild West style shooter developed by Adolfo Cirillo and released into the public domain in 1996.

456237.overview:
As you opened the ancient tomb's gates, you unknowingly triggered a mechanism that sealed you inside. Around you stretches a dark labyrinth filled with mysteries, traps, and riddles of the past. To escape to the surface, you must find crystal skulls that will unseal the closed passages. Every step is a race against time and your own fear, but somewhere in the darkness lies the path to freedom. Will you uncover the tomb's secrets and break free from its grasp?

The tomb is never the same twice—each time you enter, the artifacts are hidden in different locations, and your journey begins from a new starting point.

457621.overview: This is an implementation of the Tunnels & Trolls game (5th Edition), in its solitaire form, consisting of the game engine and 32 adventures. It allows you to play the adventures without pen, paper, dice, cards, nor the adventures themselves. The complete T&T rulebook will prove handy but is not essential.

458976.overview:
Created with AMOS Professional and intended as a loving memory of
Mr. Martyn Brown who sadly passed away recently... It is a very simple puzzle game.

459885.overview:
This is second part of my humble, yet sincere tribute to all Team17 Amiga games.
Created with AMOS Professional and intended as a loving memory of
Mr. Martyn Brown who sadly passed away in December 2024...

461765.overview: Press space to start the game. Place your fingers on the keyboard while you GET READY. When a random character is displayed on the screen, you have to press the same character on the keyboard to draw and shoot your gun! If you are too slow, or you press the wrong character, you will get wasted.

463929.overview: A 2 Player death match Tank Game played on a single screen with bouncing bullets.

472095.overview: You need at least two identical jewels to remove them from the playfield. Find 3 or more identical jewels to fill the playfield with new items. The more you can remove at once, the more new you get. The game is over if there are no more matches.

476370.overview:
This game is an adaptation of the Italian adventure Kenneth Johnson: Tin Star by Bonaventura Di Bello. It was originally published on the cover tape of Viking, no. 5, May 1987 for the Commodore 64 and ZX Spectrum.
It has now been translated to English and rewritten for a modern audience with the original author's permission. This new version includes many enhancements that weren't in the original. Type ABOUT in the game for further info.

480234.overview: A lesser known classic from Konami's MSX library now ported to the Amiga

480310.overview:
Langford Productions' Turmoil — 26 levels of oil-collecting platform action — as a native 68040 Amiga game.
Mick has oil to collect and no time to waste. Twenty-six levels of ladders, drops and hazards, with a level select, instructions and a well-done screen when you finally make it.

481537.overview: Conversion of the original arcade ROM of Tetris, 1988, Atari Games arcade board

481588.overview: It's a Lady Tut inspired game for the Amiga 500, The game is completely free, I used AI, this is version 1.0, I could improve it furthermore in the future (for now after level 3 u got infinite ammo, but next version will be corrected).

481645.overview: Time Pilot '82 for Amiga AGA based on Konami's original 1982 arcade game, my favourite title from the arcade golden age.

481667.overview: The concept is simple: stack moving blocks on top of each other and build your tower as high as possible. Timing and precision are essential — misaligned blocks will make your tower narrower, making each subsequent move more challenging!

481709.overview: This is a tongue-in-cheek Wordle clone created as a tribute to a lovely person and the best dressed streamer on Twitch on her 50th Birthday.

481795.overview: A port of the PC (MS-DOS, 256-colour VGA) version of Test Drive III to theAGA Amiga. The original 8086 game code was statically recompiled to native 68020+ code, so the polygon engine, physics and all game logic are the PC original. Graphics are the full 320x200 VGA picture in 256 colours on an AGA screen; music and sound effects come from the Tandy 3-voice sound driver, played through Paula.

481898.overview: In this game, the player controls an explorer who is robbing Tutankhamun's tomb. The player will search for precious treasures (maps, lamps, chests of gold & jewels, and, above all, the golden mask of King Tut) and fight off the various creatures that guard the tomb to ultimately find the way through the catacombs.

482059.overview: Tough Nuts is a physics slingshot game for the Amiga 1200 (AGA) in the spirit of Angry Birds, with a world of its own: nuts knock bark beetles out of their forts. Nine worlds of ten levels, nine heroes with abilities of their own, bosses, cartoons and ten tunes — on two floppies or on a hard disk.

482065.overview: A puzzle game for all Amigas.

482077.overview: Now, Tag Team Wrestling makes its Amiga debut as a nearly arcade-accurate transcode for AGA Amigas. This conversion brings the original coin-op’s distinctive wrestling action and tag-team strategy  giving Amiga players a chance to experience an early cornerstone of arcade wrestling.

482091.overview: You cannot climb, and you cannot jump. But you can tilt the whole room by 90 degrees — and everything that is not nailed down falls with it. Crates tumble, gems drop, and so do you. Collect every gem, open the glowing green exit and step through before the room turns against you.

482119.overview: Tomb Lady - Part II is a classic action-adventure maze game for the Amiga 500 (512kb) or Amiga 1000 (with the 256kb A1050 front panel expansion), loosely inspired by the 8-bit Commodore 64 classic Lady Tut. In this sequel, players guide fearless heroes through perilous, trap-filled ruins, ancient tombs, and mysterious underground caverns.

482635.overview: SEGA's 1985 arcade game, rebuilt natively for the Amiga 500. Not an emulator: Teddy Boy Blues was rewritten in 68000 assembly language, with the arcade game logic extracted from the original program and checked step by step against the arcade machine. Graphics were converted for the Amiga's display chips, music and sound effects recreated for Paula.

482876.overview: An unofficial fan port of Toaplan's 1988 vertical shooter, made by static recompilation of the original arcade program into native 68030 code. The whole game, the arcade music and the sound effects: exactly the arcade game, running on an Amiga.

482902.overview: Long ago, in the age of the Commodore 64, there was a platformer called Trolls and Tribulations. It had 32 levels of scrolling mischief, enemies lurking around every corner, and music and sound effects that buzzed out of the SID chip.
